items.title: JI sends Rs1bn defamation notice to ex-FBR chief Shabbar Zaidi
items.description: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) has sent a legal notice to former Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) chairman Shabbar Zaidi and sought Rs1 billion in damages over allegations that the party received money to suppress public protests, according to a statement by the JI. The statement said the legal notice was sent on July 27 through Advocate Tahir Iqbal Malik on the directives of the party’s Karachi General Secretary Taufiquddin Siddiqui. When Dawn contacted Zaidi for his comment on Tuesday, the former FBR chief said he had forwarded the notice to his lawyer for legal advice. The JI’s statement, citing the party’s notice, said Zaidi made serious allegations against the party during a podcast interview and subsequently in statements circulated on YouTube, Facebook, X, TikTok, WhatsApp and other social media platforms. The notice alleged that the former FBR chairman described the party as the “establishment’s firewall” for “diluting” public issues and protests. In the notice, the statement said, JI’s lawyer contended that Zaidi’s statements amounted to “serious allegations against the party, including secret funding, bribery, corruption, political deception, betrayal of public interests, and alleged collusion with state elements”. Through the notice, the JI demanded that Zaidi provides complete evidence in support of his claim, including the identity of person who allegedly made the payment; the name of person who received the money; the amount paid; the date, time and place of the payment; the method of payment; the relevant bank account or financial document; details of the alleged protest or public issue; witnesses to the transaction, documents and recordings; and the source on the basis of which the allegation was made, the statement said.

items.title: Niger : 22 morts, dont 17 militaires, dans une collision entre deux bus sur l’axe Maradi-Madaoua
items.description: Une collision entre deux autobus de transport de voyageurs a fait 22 morts et 37 blesses vendredi 7 août 2026 sur l'axe Maradi-Madaoua, au Niger. Les deux vehicules appartenaient aux compagnies SONITRAV et STM. Parmi les personnes decedees figurent 17 militaires, selon le ministere nigerien des Transports. L'accident s'est produit a hauteur de Doukou Doukou, a environ 55 kilometres de Madaoua. Dans sa premiere depeche publiee le 8 août, l'Agence Nigerienne de Presse (ANP) faisait etat d'un bilan provisoire de 21 morts et 37 blesses. Deux jours plus tard, le 10 août, le bilan actualise est passe a de 22 deces et 37 blesses. Deux bus violemment entres en collision Selon les premiers elements communiques par la gendarmerie, l'accident a implique un bus de la compagnie SONITRAV venant de Maradi, qui transportait notamment des militaires, et un vehicule de la compagnie STM venant de Madaoua. Les deux autobus se sont violemment heurtes avant de quitter leur trajectoire. Le commandant de bataillon de la gendarmerie de Madaoua, cite par l'ANP, a indique que le bus de la STM avait poursuivi sa course sur environ 170 metres, tandis que celui de SONITRAV avait parcouru environ 96 metres apres le choc. L'un des conducteurs etait decede lors de la collision, selon la meme source. Les 37 blesses ont ete pris en charge par les services sanitaires. Dans le premier bilan diffuse le 8 août, la gendarmerie indiquait que les victimes decedees avaient ete transportees a l'hopital de district de Madaoua et que les blesses avaient ete evacues vers Madaoua et Maradi, dont neuf vers Maradi. Dix-sept militaires parmi les victimes Un bilan communique par le ministere nigerien des Transports et relaye a etabli que 17 des 22 personnes decedees etaient des militaires. Le 8 août, avant la publication de ce bilan actualise, les autorites et responsables des Forces de defense et de securite de la region de Maradi avaient rendu un dernier hommage a 16 membres des Forces de defense et de securite dont les corps se trouvaient a la morgue de Maradi. Une priere mortuaire avait ete organisee avant leur inhumation au cimetiere musulman de la ville. Une enquete ouverte sur les causes de l'accident Les circonstances precises ayant conduit a la collision n'ont pas encore ete etablies publiquement. Des le 8 août, la gendarmerie avait annonce l'ouverture d'une enquete destinee a determiner les causes de l'accident. Le 10 août, le ministre des Transports et de l'Aviation civile, le colonel-major Abdouramane Amadou, a convoque les responsables des compagnies STM et SONITRAV pour une reunion consacree au drame. Selon le communique rapporte par l' ANP , les representants des deux entreprises ont ete entendus sur leurs responsabilites respectives et ont recu des instructions pour corriger les manquements constates. Le ministre a estime que le comportement humain demeure un facteur fondamental dans ce type d'accident et a denonce les comportements imprudents de certains conducteurs ainsi que l'indulgence dont leurs employeurs peuvent faire preuve. Cette appreciation generale des autorites ne constitue toutefois pas, a ce stade, une conclusion de l'enquete sur la responsabilite precise de l'une ou l'autre compagnie dans l'accident du 7 août. Des sanctions envisagees contre la compagnie qui serait reconnue responsable Le ministere des Transports a annonce que des sanctions seraient prises contre la societe dont la responsabilite serait etablie. Selon la gravite des manquements retenus, les mesures prevues peuvent aller de l'avertissement a la suspension, voire au retrait de l'agrement d'exploitation, independamment d'eventuelles poursuites judiciaires decidees par les autorites competentes. La reunion du 10 août s'est tenue en presence de responsables du ministere des Transports et de l'Aviation civile, de l'Agence Nigerienne de Securite Routiere (ANISER) et de la Gendarmerie nationale. Un drame dans un contexte de forte mortalite routiere Cette collision intervient alors que les autorites nigeriennes ont declare 2026 « Annee de la Discipline Routiere », une initiative annoncee en avril par le ministere des Transports et de l'Aviation civile afin de renforcer la securite sur les routes. Les statistiques officielles illustrent l'ampleur du probleme. Selon des donnees communiquees en avril 2026 et reprises par l'ANP, 7 116 accidents corporels ont ete enregistres au Niger en 2025, faisant 1 245 morts et 4 439 blesses graves.

items.title: Afolabi assumes duty as 35th Abia Commissioner of Police
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe UMUAHIA — The Abia State Police Command has welcomed a new Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Olutokunbo Afolabi, who has assumed duty as the 35th Commissioner of Police in the state. Afolabi takes over from AIG Danladi Isa, who was promoted and redeployed to the Force Criminal Investigation Department (FCID), Annex, Kaduna. In a statement issued on August 10, 2026, the Command’s Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Maureen Chioma Chinaka, described the new commissioner as a seasoned police officer with more than three decades of service in the Nigeria Police Force. Afolabi joined the force as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police on May 18, 1992, and has served in various strategic command, operational, administrative and international policing positions. He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Botany from the University of Ilorin, as well as a Postgraduate Diploma and a Master’s degree in Peace and Security Studies from the University of Port Harcourt. His professional training includes the Strategic Leadership and Command Course at the National Institute of Police Studies, Abuja; Tactical Leadership Command Course at the Police Staff College, Jos; Internal Security/Low Intensity Conflict Course at the Armed Forces Command and Staff College, Jaji; and Peacekeeping Negotiation Course at the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre, Ghana. Afolabi also has extensive international policing experience. Between 2004 and 2005, he served as pioneer Sector Commander of Sector 2, Nyala, and pioneer Regional Commander of Southern Darfur under the African Union Mission in Sudan. During the assignment, he helped establish operational and administrative structures, set up police stations in internally displaced persons’ camps and coordinated civil police activities. Earlier, between 2001 and 2002, he served as Nigeria Contingent Commander and Special Response Unit Officer under the Human Rights Section of the United Nations Mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where he contributed to law enforcement reforms, system analysis and training programmes for local police personnel. Before his deployment to Abia, Afolabi served as Commissioner of Police, Administration, Training and Development, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja. He had also served as Commissioner of Police in Ondo State, where he coordinated administrative and operational activities, strengthened intelligence gathering, improved investigative efficiency and promoted community policing initiatives. He also served as Commissioner of Police, Force Equitation Officer, Mounted Troop, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja, supervising mounted police operations and ensuring operational readiness and professionalism in crowd control and ceremonial duties. Between 2021 and 2023, Afolabi served as Deputy Commissioner of Police, Administration, Delta State Command; DCP, Criminal Investigation Department, Katsina State Command; and DCP, Operations, Bayelsa State Command. As DCP Administration in Delta, he handled high-level administrative responsibilities and enforcement of police regulations. In Katsina, he coordinated criminal investigations, while in Bayelsa, he planned and supervised crime prevention and operational activities across the state. Between 2016 and 2021, he served in various capacities, including Area Commander in Anambra State Command, Assistant Commissioner of Police, Operations, Imo State Command, and Assistant Commissioner of Police, Intelligence, Abuja. From 2014 to 2016, Afolabi served as a Divisional Police Officer in several divisions within the Federal Capital Territory before becoming a Directing Staff at the Police Staff College, Jos, where he trained and mentored senior police officers. His career also includes service as Sector Commander and Second-in-Command in Joint Task Force operations in Warri, Staff Officer at the Force Headquarters and Unit Commander of the Police Mobile Force in Plateau State, where he participated in specialised policing operations. Afolabi has undertaken several national and international assignments, including serving among the first Nigerian police officers deployed to the African Union Mission in Darfur. He was also the last Contingent Commander of the Nigeria Police Team to the United Nations Mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina and served as Aide-de-Camp to visiting Heads of State. He participated in the organisation of major international events, including the All African Games and Commonwealth Summit. Afolabi is a Fellow of the Peace and Security Studies Department of the University of Port Harcourt and a Justice of the Peace. The Command described him as a disciplined, strategic and result-oriented police officer whose career reflects a commitment to public safety, professional excellence and international policing standards. It called on stakeholders, traditional and community leaders, civil society organisations and members of the public to extend their cooperation to the new commissioner as he begins his tenure. According to the Command, such cooperation would be critical to Afolabi’s efforts to strengthen security, improve policing and safeguard lives and property across Abia State. Afolabi is married with children. His hobbies include travelling and reading. The post Afolabi assumes duty as 35th Abia Commissioner of Police appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bintou Signate et Mouhamadou Nazirou Diankha veulent révolutionner la seconde main au Sénégal
items.description: Tekkofi entend bousculer les habitudes de vente entre particuliers. Avec ses annonces vocales, l’absence de commission et sa messagerie intégrée, elle veut offrir une alternative aux échanges dispersés sur les réseaux sociaux, tout en misant sur l’économie circulaire et les usages locaux. Acheter un meuble, un vêtement ou encore un appareil électronique répond à un besoin. Mais dans certains cas, ils finissent souvent au placard ou sur le toit d’une terrasse. C’est ce constat qui a poussé Bintou Signate et Mouhamadou Nazirou Diankha a créé « Tekkofi ». Lancée le 11 juillet 2026, cette plateforme qui compte plus d’une centaine d'utilisateurs vise à donner une seconde vie à un objet et aide à trouver facilement ce dont on a besoin. « Un particulier peut vendre un objet pour générer un revenu complémentaire ou choisir de le donner. Un professionnel peut présenter son activité, développer sa visibilité et toucher de nouveaux clients. Le tout dans un environnement simple, sécurisé et pensé pour les habitudes des utilisateurs sénégalais. Avec Mouhamadou Nazirou Diankha, nous avons voulu construire une plateforme qui réponde à tous ces besoins », a expliqué Bintou Signate.À l’en croire, Tekkofi n'est pas seulement une plateforme de petites annonces. C'est une façon de repenser notre manière de consommer, de vendre, de partager et de créer de la valeur à partir de ce que nous possédons déjà. Le choix du nom Tekkofi est le reflet meme de l'identité que les deux concepteurs veulent donner à la plateforme.« En wolof, il signifie « pose-le ici ». Cette expression traduit parfaitement l'idée de la plateforme : un espace où chacun peut déposer quelque chose, un objet à vendre ou à donner, un produit à présenter, un service à proposer, ou simplement une opportunité à partager. C'est un lieu d'échange où ce qui est déposé peut trouver une nouvelle valeur auprès d'une autre personne », a expliqué Bintou. Cette dernière précise également que le choix du nom est aussi une référence sonore à « take coffee » en anglais. « Le café évoque un moment simple et convivial : un espace où les personnes se rencontrent, échangent et créent des liens. Cette dimension représente notre ambition de faire de Tekkofi plus qu'un outil numérique : un espace de connexion entre les personnes avec des ambitions internationales », a-t-elle relevé. Ni WhatsApp encore moins Tiktok Tekkofi n’est pas Facebook encore moins WhatsApp. C’est ce que souligne Bintou Signate.« Ces outils ont permis à de nombreux vendeurs, entrepreneurs et particuliers de commencer à présenter leurs produits sur Internet. Cependant, ils fonctionnent principalement à partir d'un réseau existant », nuance Bintou. Sur WhatsApp Business, poursuit-elle, pour découvrir les produits d'un vendeur, il faut généralement déjà connaître son numéro ou l'avoir déjà dans ses contacts. Cela limite naturellement la visibilité des vendeurs : un commerçant peut avoir de bons produits, mais rester invisible auprès de personnes qui ne connaissent pas encore son activité ou l'avoir déjà dans ses contacts. « Avec Tekkofi, nous avons voulu inverser cette logique. La plateforme permet aux utilisateurs de découvrir des produits et des services au-delà de leur propre réseau. Un acheteur peut rechercher un article, comparer plusieurs offres et trouver un vendeur sans avoir besoin de connaître son numéro de téléphone au préalable », renseigne la cofondatrice de Tekkofi. Tekkofi possède également une fonctionnalité d’annonce vocale. Cela rend la plateforme accessible à ceux qui sont peu à l'aise avec l'écrit.« En sus de cela, il y a le 0% de commission, qui garantit aux vendeurs de garder l'intégralité de leurs gains ainsi que la messagerie interne, qui protège la vie privée des utilisateurs. C'est une plateforme pensée par des Sénégalais, pour les réalités sénégalaises », insiste-t-elle. Cette dernière souligne aussi que la plateforme a été pensé autour des réalités de la seconde main.« Beaucoup de personnes ont aujourd'hui des objets qu'elles n'utilisent plus et qui pourraient être utiles à d'autres. La plateforme leur permet de vendre, mais aussi de donner une seconde vie à ces objets », explique-t-elle. Seconde main, seconde vie « Nous accumulons des objets, des vêtements, des appareils électroniques ou du mobilier qui finissent souvent oubliés dans un placard ou un garage. Pourtant, ils ont encore de la valeur et pourraient être utiles à d'autres. Dans le même temps, de nombreuses personnes recherchent des alternatives plus abordables pour s'équiper, tandis que d'autres souhaitent consommer de manière plus responsable en privilégiant la seconde main », constate Bintou. À l’en croire, c’est justement ces observations qui ont motivé la création de Tekkofi. « Notre ambition n'est pas de remplacer les outils que les Sénégalais utilisent déjà, mais de proposer un espace complémentaire, plus structuré et pensé pour leurs besoins : rechercher, comparer, acheter, vendre, donner et développer une activité », a fait savoir Bintou. Au-delà de l'aspect économique, enchaine-t-elle, l’objectif est pour eux de contribuer à faire évoluer notre manière de consommer en encourageant une logique d'économie circulaire.« Aujourd’hui, avec Tekkofi, nous voulons l donner une seconde vie aux objets en facilitant leur circulation entre les personnes », milite-t-elle. Bintou Signate explique que chaque article vendu ou donné sur la plateforme représente un objet qui continue d'être utile, et potentiellement un achat neuf évité. Cela permet de limiter le gaspillage, de prolonger la durée de vie des produits et de réduire l'impact environnemental lié à la production de nouveaux biens. « Cette approche rejoint plusieurs Objectifs de Développement Durable des Nations Unies, notamment l'ODD 12 sur la consommation et la production responsables, qui encourage une utilisation plus durable des ressources et la réduction des déchets. Elle s'inscrit également dans une réflexion plus large autour de l'ODD 11 sur les villes et communautés durables, en favorisant des modes de consommation plus responsables au sein des territoires », soutient Bintou. La cofondatrice de Tekkofi rappelle aussi que dans le contexte sénégalais, où les pratiques de réutilisation, de partage et de transmission existent déjà depuis longtemps, leur ambition est d'utiliser le numérique pour renforcer ces dynamiques et leur donner une nouvelle échelle. « Nous ne prétendons pas résoudre à nous seuls les enjeux environnementaux, mais nous voulons contribuer à un changement progressif des habitudes : acheter autrement, vendre ce qui n'est plus utilisé, donner plutôt que jeter, et considérer chaque objet comme une ressource qui peut encore créer de la valeur », ambitionne-t-elle. « Nous ne comptons pas nous arrêter en si bon chemin. Notre ambition est de construire une plateforme qui accompagne l'utilisateur tout au long de son parcours : trouver un produit, échanger avec un vendeur, finaliser un achat et, à terme, faciliter davantage la transaction », annonce Bintou Signate. Mais la jeune femme souligne que leur ambition dépasse nos frontières.« Dans cinq ans, nous voulons que Tekkofi soit une plateforme africaine de référence pour la vente entre particuliers et professionnels, reconnue pour son accessibilité et sa proximité avec les usages réels des populations. Une technologie qui se sera adaptée à ses utilisateurs, et non l'inverse », souhaite-t-elle. Des ambitions ancrées entre ouverture et enracinement. Arame NDIAYE

items.title: « Le Sénégal est le territoire de la littérature féminine, et de la réflexion »
items.description: Alain Mabanckou, Grand Prix de littérature Henri Gal de l’Académie française qui récompense l’ensemble de son œuvre, rend hommage au Sénégal et à ses grandes personnalités des Lettres. GENÈVE – Alain Mabanckou a rendu hommage au Sénégal et à sa littérature, dans un entretien exclusif, à la Société de Lecture de Genève, bastion de la littérature mondiale, fondée en 1818, dans les pures traditions des sociétés de lecture du siècle des Lumières. L’écrivain congolais est venu y présenter son dernier roman, « Ramsès de Paris » (Le Seuil). Pour Pr Mabanckou, les grands textes de la littérature africaine viennent de ces grands auteurs qu’ont été les Senghor, Cheikh Hamidou Kane, jusqu’aux nouvelles générations comme ses « petits frères », notamment Mohamed Mbougar Sarr. « J’ai toujours aussi apprécié, de près ou de loin, le fait que le Sénégal ait été à la pointe de la littérature féminine, en ces années 70 », dit-il. Dans cette décennie 1970-1980, nous avons Mariama Bâ qui fait « Une si longue lettre »,avant plus tard « La grève des bàttu » et « Le jujubier du patriarche » d’Aminata Sow Fall, etc. « Le Sénégal a porté le féminisme littéraire à un sommet rare », souligne l’auteur. Dans ce sens, beaucoup ne rendent certainement pas justice à cette littérature car, au fond, des femmes comme Ken Bugul ou d’autres écrivaines ouest-africaines comme Véronique Tadjo (Côte d’Ivoire), analyse l’auteur, si elles écrivent, aujourd’hui, c’est qu’il y a eu les Aminata Sow Fall, les Mariama Bâ, etc. Le Sénégal est le territoire de la littérature féminine mais aussi le territoire de la réflexion avec « L’Aventure ambiguë » de Cheikh Hamidou Kane, de la poésie avec Léopold Sédar Senghor et des plus grands poèmes d’Afrique comme « Souffles » in « Leurres et Lueurs (Présence Africaine, 1960) de Birago Diop et ses « Comptes d’Ahmadou Kumba (1947). (Ndlr : Il récite de mémoire « Souffles », poème intemporel !). Interrogés sur les propos de l’écrivain congolais, la professeure Ndiémé Sow de l’Université Ahmadou Mactar Mbow souligne: « c'est un message émouvant d'un grand professeur qui symbolise la littérature panafricaine, qui connaît parfaitement la littéraire sénégalaise, à travers les âges, les sexes et les genres. « Il a une excellente culture de la littérature Sénégalaise » renchérit son collègue le professeur Moustapha Mbengue de l'Ebad. L’écrivaine sénégalaise, Nafissatou Dia, se réjouit: « C’est un bel hommage à notre littérature et à nos grands auteurs ». Ce qui fait dire au professeur Ibrahima Wane de l’Ucad : « C’est un témoignage très important qui rappelle le leadership historique du Sénégal sur le plan culturel ». Fils unique, issu du quartier de Voungou, à Pointe-Noire (Congo-Brazzaville), Alain Mabanckou, l’enfant solitaire qui se parlait à lui-même, a transformé, en grandissant, ses monologues en un grand village littéraire mondial qui séduit au-delà de l’espace francophone. La maman du professeur-écrivain voulait que son unique enfant soit avocat ou juge, convaincue que cela « lui permettrait notamment d’obtenir une meilleure place au marché où elle est vendeuse d’arachides ». Littérature et poésie contre plaidoirie L’enfant s’exécuta et entreprit des études de droit. Il obtient, à 22 ans, une bourse et s’envole pour Paris. « Ses cahiers de poésie sous le bras », la fidélité au vœu de la maman est rompue à la mort de cette dernière alors qu’Alain entamait pourtant le Certificat d’aptitude à la profession d’avocat. Le feu de l’écriture brûlait l’enfant de Pointe Noire qui, après un stage juridique dans le groupe Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux, publie son premier roman, Bleu-Blanc-Rouge (1998). Alors que l’Equipe de France remporte la Coupe du monde de football, le Congolais est sacré Grand Prix Littéraire de l’Afrique noire. Il a vite développé un amour pour la poésie. Il lisait des poèmes et en écrivait, notamment à ses conquêtes amoureuses de l’époque. « Il lui arrivait de rédiger le même poème à trois personnes différentes, mais en changeant simplement de nom à chaque fois ». Il avait bien compris que le poète était là pour charmer, selon l’avocate Caroline Turrettini, en présentant Alain Mabanckou et son dernier roman « Ramsès de Paris », qui suit le destin de Berado, prince de Zamunda, qui a quitté le Congo pour rejoindre à Paris son mentor, Benoît, autre Congolais! « Une célébration de l’universalité de l’exil et la beauté des sentiments humains ». Une sorte d’autobiographie de l’un des plus grands intellectuels congolais de notre temps. C’est son père adoptif, dit-on, qui lui fait découvrir la lecture. Ce dernier travaillait en tant que réceptionniste dans un hôtel à Pointe-Noire et des touristes européens laissaient souvent derrière eux, en rentrant, leurs livres qui ne rentraient pas dans les malles, rappelle Turrettini. « Son père les récupérait et les ramenait à la maison dans l’espoir de les lire lorsqu’il prendrait sa retraite ». Il lui était interdit de s’en approcher, mais dès que le père avait le dos tourné, Alain en profitait pour plonger le nez dedans. Mabanckou dit qu’il pensait qu’il fallait lire les livres dans l’ordre alphabétique, et que s’il lui arrivait à lire Zola, il aurait lu tous les livres du monde. Alain Mabanckou a 60 ans. Il semble ne pas les faire avec son allure de « sapé comme jamais » et son rire de tonnerre. Cet écrivain est « un monument de talents, d’intelligence, d’humour et de sagesse. Il charrie en lui l’âme de l’Afrique. C’est un homme charismatique et flamboyant : toujours bien sapé sans afficher de marques ostentatoires ; il arbore autant les couleurs vives sur lui qu’en lui », nous confie Emmanuel Tagnard, directeur culturel de la Société de Lecture. Professeur de littérature française à l’Université de Californie/Los Angeles (Ucla) depuis 20 ans, il est l’une des grandes voix de l’Afrique francophone aux États-Unis. « Il cherche toujours à explorer et valoriser ses propres racines tout en étant ouvert et curieux des autres communautés. Sa langue est riche d’originalité et d’enseignements », poursuit Tagnard. «Outre les différents couvre-chefs qu’il porte chaque jour, il est décidément un homme aux multiples casquettes ». La plupart de ses romans sont imprégnés de sa langue maternelle et de sa culture africaine. Il reste très engagé dans la perception que l’on a de la littérature africaine. « Il lutte contre cette ghettoïsation, entre la littérature française et la littérature francophone ». En 2016, il est le premier écrivain à intégrer la chaire de création artistique du Collège de France. Il y enseigne l’Afrique, son histoire et sa littérature. Inédit. Là encore, c’est un succès, car le premier cours qu’il y donne rassemble plus de 1.500 personnes. Ses huit leçons ont été reprises et publiées en 2021 par les éditions Grasset sous le titre Huit leçons sur l’Afrique. Les États-Unis, c’est un coin depuis lequel Alain Mabanckou regarde « les empreintes de ses errances ». En 2022, il se lance dans un nouveau projet, le documentaire. Scénariste et acteur, il prête sa voix au film « Noirs en France » qui a été le documentaire le plus vu cette année-là (+7 millions de téléspectateurs sur France2). Alain Mabanckou est auteur de plus de quatorze romans dont « Verre Cassé » (2005), « Mémoires de porc-épic » (prix Renaudot en 2006), « Demain j’aurai vingt ans » (Prix George Brassens en 2010), « Lumières de Pointe-Noire », ou encore « Petit piment » en 2015 (finaliste de l’International Booker Prize). Par El Hadji Gorgui Wade NDOYE (Correspondant permanent)

items.title: NACSA educates students on firearm safety and gun violence prevention
items.description: The National Commission on Small Arms and Light Weapons (NACSA) has intensified efforts to educate young people on firearm safety and gun violence prevention through school-based public education programmes. The Commission recently engaged students of Nungua Senior High School in the Greater Accra Region and Ghana Senior High School (GHANASS) in the Eastern Region, where participants received practical education on firearm safety, preventing gun violence and responsible citizenship. According to the Commission in a social media post on Monday, August 10, the sessions sought to help students understand how peer influence, exposure to firearms and unresolved conflicts could contribute to unsafe situations in schools and communities. Students were encouraged to make responsible choices, avoid violent behaviour and seek appropriate assistance when confronted with suspicious activities, firearms-related incidents or potential threats. NACSA said young people had an important role to play in efforts to prevent gun violence and promote safer communities. The Commission noted that equipping students with the knowledge to identify risks and respond appropriately could help reduce exposure to firearm-related dangers in schools and communities. Through the school-based engagements, NACSA is positioning young people as active partners in promoting peace, responsible citizenship and safer school environments.

items.title: El fuego sigue activo en Niebla: “Es un incendio al que todavía le quedan días de trabajo”
items.description: El incendio de Niebla (Huelva) sigue activo este martes tras afectar a más de 20.000 hectáreas y mantener desalojadas a 700 personas de los municipios de Niebla, Berrocal, Villarasa, Zalamea la Real y El Madroño. El consejero de Presidencia, Sanidad y Emergencias de la Junta de Andalucía, Antonio Sanz, ha subrayado esta mañana que la noche ha permitido contener las llamas en algunos puntos, pero que aún queda mucho por hacer. “ Es un incendio al que todavía le quedan días de trabajo porque la extensión y perímetro son todavía muy grandes. Hay que actuar sobre muchos kilómetros y hay que trabajar metro a metro para sellar y evitar nuevas reactivaciones”, ha informado Sanz desde el puesto de mando avanzado. Seguir leyendo

items.title: GES opens 17th National Festival of Arts and Culture for Basic Schools in Techiman
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has commenced the 17th National Festival of Arts and Culture for Basic Schools in Techiman in the Bono East Region, bringing together young talents from all 16 regions to showcase Ghana’s rich cultural heritage. The five-day festival, which began on Sunday, August 9, 2026, and ends on Thursday, August 13, is being organised through the GES Arts and Culture Department. Activities are being held at Our Lady of Mount Carmel Girls’ Senior High School and Techiman Senior High School, where 16 cultural troupes representing the regions are showcasing their talents in music, dance, drama, poetry, costumes and other forms of artistic expression. The opening ceremony on Monday, August 10, brought together education officials, teachers, pupils, traditional authorities, dignitaries and members of the public. The Bono East Regional Minister was represented at the ceremony by the Municipal Chief Executive for Kintampo North, Isaac Donkor, while the Bono East Regional Director of Education, Rev. Kingsley Gyamina Asante, also attended. The ceremony was chaired by Nana Apinteng Foso Gyabuo II, who joined other stakeholders in highlighting the importance of arts and culture in the education and development of young people. The festival has attracted large numbers of basic school pupils, who have gathered to support their colleagues and witness the various cultural performances and displays. Beyond competition, the National Festival of Arts and Culture provides a platform for promoting national unity, cultural identity and creativity among young people. It also enables pupils from different parts of the country to interact, learn from one another and develop a deeper appreciation of Ghana’s diverse cultural traditions and values. The GES said initiatives such as the festival form part of efforts to promote holistic education by nurturing creativity, confidence, discipline and a strong sense of national identity among learners. As the festival continues, participants are expected to take part in further cultural performances, artistic displays and competitions as they showcase their talents and celebrate Ghana’s cultural heritage.

items.title: El Mourouj | Il jette ses deux fillettes du 3e étage
items.description: C’est à peine croyable : un fonctionnaire, âgé d’une quarantaine d’années, a jeté ses deux fillettes depuis le troisième étage d’un immeuble résidentiel à El Mourouj 1, au sud des Tunis. Cela s’est passé lundi 10 août 2026, a rapporté Diwan FM , en citant une source de police. Le drame a entraîné le décès de l’une des deux fillettes, âgée de six mois, tandis que sa sœur, âgée de trois ans, a été transférée au service de réanimation dans un état critique. Les forces de police ont procédé à l’arrestation du père, un fonctionnaire marié depuis huit ans. Au moment des faits, l’épouse était au travail. Le ministère public a ordonné la mise en garde à vue du père et l’ouverture d’une enquête pour déterminer les mobiles et les circonstances de cet incident. L’article El Mourouj | Il jette ses deux fillettes du 3e étage est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Inuwa intensifies push for federal road projects, meets Umahi
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has intensified efforts to attract Federal Government intervention in major road projects across the state, particularly those considered critical to agricultural, commercial, industrial and tourism development. Yahaya renewed the push during a meeting with the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, on Monday in Abuja, where he canvassed accelerated action on strategic federal road projects in the state. According to a statement by the Director-General, Press Affairs, Government House, Gombe, Ismaila Uba Misilli, the meeting formed part of the governor’s sustained engagements with the Federal Government to improve road connectivity and unlock economic opportunities across the state. A major focus of the meeting was the Gombe-Biu axis of the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Gombe-Biu-Maiduguri Super Highway, recently approved and flagged off by the Federal Government. Yahaya has consistently advocated the early commencement of work on the Gombe-Biu section, describing the corridor as strategically important to Gombe and the entire North-East. His advocacy has included repeated engagements with the Ministry of Works and other relevant federal authorities, culminating in Umahi’s recent visit to Gombe, where he joined the governor and members of the National Assembly for the groundbreaking ceremony of the project. Following the groundbreaking, the governor is seeking sustained momentum towards the commencement of full-scale construction and timely completion of the road. Another major request by the governor is the construction of northern and southern bypasses for Gombe metropolis. According to Yahaya, the proposed bypasses would open up the state capital from both ends, create strategic links to the Gombe-Biu corridor, decongest existing roads and facilitate the movement of people and goods. Responding, Umahi described the Gombe-Biu axis of the super highway as a priority project of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu administration, assuring the governor that his request for construction to commence from the proposed point of interest would be given due consideration. The minister also expressed confidence in the capacity of Hitech Construction Company, the contractor handling the project, describing it as one of the competent firms executing major infrastructure projects in the country. Umahi commended Yahaya for his persistence and commitment to pursuing development projects for the people of Gombe State. Reflecting on his recent visit to the state, the minister said the experience had deepened his appreciation of the scale and quality of infrastructure development under the Yahaya administration. “Since my visit to Gombe, I have become like your ambassador. Anywhere I go, I talk about your state and the developmental strides I have witnessed. I tell people, when you want to see genuine development and visionary leadership, go to Gombe,” Umahi said. He assured the governor that the Federal Government would deliver the project, expressing optimism that its completion would have a significant impact on the people of Gombe and further demonstrate the infrastructure agenda of the Tinubu administration. The minister also acknowledged Yahaya’s sustained advocacy for the rehabilitation and reconstruction of other strategic highways linking Gombe with neighbouring states and economic centres. They include the Gombe-Bajoga-Potiskum, Gombe-Dukku-Darazo and Gombe-Bauchi corridors. The roads, which connect several communities and agricultural areas to major markets and commercial centres, are regarded as critical economic links for Gombe State and the wider North-East. The governor’s renewed push is expected to strengthen federal-state collaboration on road infrastructure, improve regional connectivity and create new opportunities for trade, agriculture, investment and industrial development across the state. items.title: Why I am supporting Donkemezuo for House of Reps — Dokubo-Asari
items.description: By Adesina Wahab Da Amakiri Tubo, Alhaji Mujahid Abubakr Dokubo-Asari, Amanyanabo of The Source, Elem Kalabari, Torusarama Piri, has explained his decision to support the aspiration of Hon. Engr. Elvis Donkemezuo to represent Yenagoa–Kolokuma/Opokuma Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives in 2027. Dokubo-Asari, who publicly endorsed the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate during an event in Abuja on Monday, said Donkemezuo had been involved in the struggle for the advancement of the Ijaw people and understood the challenges confronting the Niger Delta. “He has fought alongside me for the Ijaw cause; he understands our struggle and will give the Ijaw people a voice in Abuja,” he said. The endorsement was made during a gathering of prominent Ijaw sons in Abuja, where Donkemezuo paid homage to the monarch and formally presented his political ambition. The meeting, which began as a traditional courtesy visit, provided an opportunity for the two men to reflect on their involvement, in different capacities, in the struggle for the rights and development of the Ijaw people. Following introductions by Prince Jude Tabai, Dokubo-Asari spoke about Donkemezuo’s record and his involvement in the Ijaw struggle. He described Donkemezuo as “a great son of Ijaw land,” recalling his participation in efforts aimed at advancing the interests and welfare of the Ijaw people. Dokubo-Asari said the 2027 election should not be viewed solely from the perspective of party politics, stressing that the Ijaw people needed representatives at the National Assembly who understood their history, challenges and aspirations. He expressed confidence that Donkemezuo had the experience and understanding required to effectively represent the people at the National Assembly. “With people like Engr. Elvis, who are conversant with the problems of the Ijaw people, the voice of the Ijaws and our challenges will be heard in the National Assembly,” he said. Donkemezuo’s Ijaw activism Donkemezuo was the pioneer coordinator of the Ijaw Youth Council (IYC), Abuja Chapter, and later served as president of the IYC in 2013. He was also involved in processes surrounding the establishment of the Presidential Amnesty Programme for former Niger Delta militants and has advocated environmental protection, justice and development in the Niger Delta. His memoir, The Vain Ijaw Struggle, chronicles his experiences during the Niger Delta struggle and the efforts to draw international attention to environmental degradation, injustice and socio-economic challenges in the region. ‘I will support you’ Dokubo-Asari also pledged his support for Donkemezuo’s political ambition, saying he would use his words and actions to support the aspiration and work towards his emergence in 2027. The monarch further prayed for divine guidance, protection, wisdom and strength for Donkemezuo as he embarks on his political journey. Also present at the gathering was Chief Ebikabowei Victor-Ben, popularly known as Boyloaf, who described Donkemezuo as “trusted and tested” and pledged his support for the aspiration. Others in attendance included Hon. Chief Raphael Kuku, Elder Edward Alagoa, a pioneer founding member of IYC Abuja, Tuedere Victor Ben, Hon. Romeo Bekeyai and Prince Jude Tabai, among others. The gathering brought together prominent figures associated with the Ijaw struggle and underscored the growing political attention surrounding the 2027 contest for the Yenagoa–Kolokuma/Opokuma Federal Constituency. The post Why I am supporting Donkemezuo for House of Reps — Dokubo-Asari appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le secteur des transports accélère la préparation
items.description: À moins de trois mois du coup d’envoi des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026, les autorités renforcent le suivi des dispositifs de transport devant accompagner l’événement. Une revue stratégique a été organisée lundi 10 août à Diamniadio par le ministre des Transports terrestres et aériens Abdoul Ahad Ndiaye pour évaluer l’état d’avancement des actions engagées dans les domaines de la mobilité terrestre et aérienne. La rencontre a réuni les principaux acteurs impliqués dans la préparation du dispositif de mobilité des JOJ. Le CETUD, Dakar Dem Dikk, l’ANASER, les ADS, l’AIBD, Air Sénégal, GTS, SENTER et l’ANACIM, entre autres, ont pris part aux échanges aux côtés d’une délégation du Comité d’organisation des JOJ Dakar 2026 (COJOJ). L’objectif est de procéder à une revue globale des actions conduites par les services du ministère et leurs partenaires, mais également de mesurer le niveau de préparation à l’approche de l’événement. Au cours de l’atelier, le ministre a appelé à maintenir un suivi rapproché des différentes opérations afin de respecter les échéances fixées. L’enjeu est notamment de s’assurer que les dispositifs prévus dans les secteurs terrestre et aérien soient pleinement opérationnels au moment de l’ouverture des Jeux. La réunion a également permis d’identifier les points nécessitant une attention particulière et de renforcer la coordination entre les différentes structures mobilisées. Une étape importante alors que le Sénégal entre dans la dernière ligne droite de la préparation des JOJ Dakar 2026. A.N

items.title: 2027: Kogi Central PDP inaugurates campaign council, names Etudaiye DG
items.description: …As Natasha says campaign must be house-to-house By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Kogi Central chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, has inaugurated its campaign organisation for the 2027 general elections, with a charge to members to take the party’s campaign to the grassroots. The campaign council was inaugurated in Okene under the leadership of Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, who represents Kogi Central in the Senate. The development was contained in a statement issued by her Media Aide, Sam Idoko, in Abuja on Tuesday. According to the statement, Dr Salami Etudaiye was appointed Director-General of the campaign, while Hon. Alhaji Abubakar Yahaya Karaku will serve as Campaign Chairman. Other members of the campaign team are Hon. Jacob Ogirima Anebe, Secretary; Hon. Ilyasu Zubair, Head of Operations; Hon. Isiaka Uhuanaye, Head of Technicals; and Hon. Jane Onoba, Head of Welfare. Speaking at the inauguration, Senator Natasha charged members of the campaign council to focus on winning the election, stressing that victory must begin at the grassroots. She said the campaign must be taken directly to voters through house-to-house and polling-unit-to-polling-unit mobilisation. “This campaign must be house-to-house and polling-unit-by-polling-unit. We must reach our people directly, listen to them, engage them and explain clearly why the PDP remains the best platform for the development and progress of our people,” she said. The senator said the party’s doors remained open to new members, urging supporters to work together to build a stronger political movement in the district. “We must open our doors for everyone who wants to join this moving train and this winning team. There is room for everyone who believes in the PDP and in the future we are building for Kogi Central,” she said. She also urged members of the campaign organisation to maintain discipline and unity while ensuring full coverage of all wards and polling units. “The election ahead will take all of us — leaders, women, youths, ward executives, coordinators, volunteers. We must work as one,” she said. In his acceptance speech, the campaign Director-General, Dr Etudaiye, described his appointment as a responsibility that required commitment and determination. “I stand before you today with a heart full of gratitude and a spirit on fire. I accept, with humility and with steely resolve, the sacred responsibility you have placed upon me as Director-General of this campaign. “This is not a ceremonial title. This is a call to battle. I did not accept this assignment to manage a campaign of polite handshakes and quiet meetings. I accepted it to organise a movement,” he said. Etudaiye said the campaign organisation would reach every part of Kogi Central, including Okene, Adavi, Ajaokuta, Okehi and Ogori-Magongo, as well as streets, markets, campuses and homes. “We are not going into this election to beg. We are going in to win and to win decisively,” he said. He urged women and youths to play leading roles in the campaign, particularly in grassroots and digital mobilisation. “To our youth: your energy, your digital power, your courage — this campaign will be incomplete without you. Come and own it,” he said. Etudaiye pledged to lead the campaign with transparency and competence, with a focus on securing votes for the party. “I will listen. I will coordinate. I will fight for every vote,” he said. “This is not just a campaign. This is a revolution of hope for Kogi Central. I accept this charge. I embrace this duty. And by the grace of God and the collective will of our people, we shall prevail,” he added. The Campaign Chairman, Karaku, urged members to put aside personal interests and differences and work towards the collective objective of strengthening the PDP and securing victory for its candidates. “This is the time for every member of our great party to come together. We must put aside whatever differences we may have and concentrate on the larger objective of building a stronger PDP and securing victory for our candidates,” he said. Karaku urged the campaign team to promote positive and issue-based messaging while strengthening its grassroots mobilisation. “Our message must be positive, our conduct must be responsible, and our mobilisation must be strategic. We must convince the people through our programmes, our commitment and our presence at the grassroots. “Elections are won by organisation, unity and the ability to connect with the people,” he said. He urged members to work collectively, stressing that every vote, ward and polling unit mattered. “Nobody should consider himself or herself too important to work with another person. Every vote matters, every ward matters and every polling unit matters. If we remain united, disciplined and focused, we can achieve the victory we desire,” Karaku said. He also appealed to party members and supporters to promote peace and issue-based politics throughout the election period. Campaign Council Director-General: Dr Salami Etudaiye Campaign Chairman: Hon. Alhaji Abubakar Yahaya Karaku Secretary: Hon. Jacob Ogirima Anebe Head of Operations: Hon. Ilyasu Zubair Head of Technicals: Hon. Isiaka Uhuanaye Head of Welfare: Hon. Jane Onoba The post 2027: Kogi Central PDP inaugurates campaign council, names Etudaiye DG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Última hora del terremoto en Colombia, en directo | Continúan durante la noche las labores de rescate de los cientos de desaparecidos
items.description: Al menos 132 personas han muerto y cientos han resultado heridas en Colombia por el terremoto de magnitud 7,4 que ha sacudido el oeste del país este lunes a las 7.34 de la mañana hora local (14.34, hora peninsular española), según el último balance entregado por la Asociación Colombiana de Ciudades Capitales. El Servicio Geológico Colombiano ha registrado 47 réplicas hasta las 18:30 (1:30 de la madrugada del día siguiente, hora peninsular española). Desde este organismo advierten que “es probable” que se registren más. Aunque la magnitud máxima que han alcanzado es de 4,8, “baja comparada con el sismo principal”. El presidente colombiano, Abelardo de la Espriella, ha cifrado en más de 1.500 las viviendas afectadas y ha elevado a 61 el número de edificios completamente colapsados. De la Espriella ha cifrado en 188 personas los desaparecidos en Cali y ha explicado que continúan las labores de búsqueda y rescate de los supervivientes durante la noche. Gran parte de los fallecidos se concentra en el área metropolitana de Pereira y también se han producido graves destrozos en la ciudad de Cali. Los aeropuertos de Cali, Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago y Buenaventura han suspendido sus operaciones. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Le Cameroun renforce la diversification des partenaires pour améliorer son système de la santé
items.description: © DR Le ministre de la Santé publique Malachie Manaouda vient de recevoir l'ambassadeur de Turquie, Volkan Öskiper et l'ambassadeur et d'Israël au Cameroun, Amnon Kalmar. Au menu des échanges, l’amélioration du système de santé et des conditions de prise en charge des patients. Les deux passages au ministère de la Santé publique sont prometteurs. L'ambassadeur d'Israël, S.E Amnon Kalmar porte le projet de son pays, partenaire du Cameroun, de rénover et de moderniser l'hôpital de district d'Essong dans la commune d'Obala. Ledit projet prévoit ainsi la réhabilitation des infrastructures, l'installation de panneaux solaires, l'acquisition du nouveau matériel de pédiatrie, de maternité et de radiologie. En outre, lors de l'inauguration de la formation sanitaire rénovée, les spécialistes du Cameroun et d'Israël vont dispenser des soins de santé gratuits. Ce volet social comprend aussi la distribution des fournitures scolaires aux enfants. Le gouvernement, par le biais du ministre de la Santé publique, Malachie Manaouda, a approuvé le projet israélien au profit de la formation sanitaire d'Essong au cours d’une audience le 10 aout dernier. Reste à présent, la mise en œuvre de l’initiative au bénéfice des populations et du système de santé camerounais. Dans le cadre de l'amélioration du même système de santé, le Cameroun et la Turquie, un autre partenaire, entendent renforcer leur partenariat médical. L'ambassadeur d'Israël au Cameroun, S.E Volkan Öskiper et le ministre de la Santé publique Malachie Manaouda ont échangé le 10 août dernier au ministère à propos de la signature d'un mémorandum d'entente. Le partenariat, d'après le ministère de la Santé publique, va apporter des changements dans la collaboration entre les deux pays. Le mémorandum va déclencher la traduction en actions concrètes sur le terrain des idées de projets. Ce sera dans le cadre de la formation continue des personnels de santé, le partage d'expertise médicale, le développement de nouveaux axes stratégiques et innovants de coopération. Tout devrait concourir à l'avenir, à ficeler des termes d'un partenariat gagnant-gagnant au bénéfice de l'amélioration de la qualité des soins et de la prise en charge médicale des patients au Cameroun. Cet article Le Cameroun renforce la diversification des partenaires pour améliorer son système de la santé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: ‘I WANT TO BE A NURSE’: Trafficked Delta girl finds hope after escaping Abidjan prostitution ring
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi For 19-year-old Annabel, the dream of becoming a nurse was almost swallowed by a journey that took her from her community in Delta State to the streets of Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, where she was trafficked into prostitution. Today, that dream is alive again. After weeks of uncertainty and abandonment in a foreign land, Annabel is back home in Ovwiamuge, Agbarho, Ughelli South Local Government Area, Delta State, reunited with her parents and receiving support to rebuild her life and return to school. Rescue Her rescue began with a viral video. In the footage, which circulated widely on social media, an unidentified interviewer found the young Nigerian on the streets of Abidjan and began asking questions to establish her identity and trace her family. “Annabel,” she replied when asked her name. She identified her state as Delta and her village as Ovwiamuge. Her parents, she said, were both alive and still in Nigeria. But there was a painful revelation: they did not know she was in Côte d’Ivoire. Asked whether she knew the people who had taken her there, Annabel indicated that she could identify her “Madam” and had her phone number. She also knew the place where she had been taken, although she did not know its name. Firm resolve The narrator explained that Annabel had been taken to Côte d’Ivoire for prostitution but was thrown out after she refused to yield. “I was told I was coming to earn from a decent job,” she said. The narrator’s appeal was simple: share the video and help locate her family. That triggered a chain of community intervention that eventually brought the teenager home. Among those who championed her return was Stella Okotete, Executive Director of Business Development at the Nigerian Export-Import Bank, who received Annabel back in Nigeria through her Erhuvwuoghene Girl Child Right Foundation. Homecoming For Okotete, the rescue could not end with bringing Annabel across the border. The bigger task was helping her recover, reintegrate into society, and reclaim a future that trafficking had threatened to destroy. “Thank God, Annabel has returned home safely. Her joyful homecoming is a moment of relief, gratitude, and hope for all of us. •Stella Okotete (bespectacled) of ErhuvwuOghene Foundation addressing Ovwiamuge residents who came in numbers to welcome their daughter back home. “This incident reminds us that the responsibility of protecting our children rests with every parent, guardian, and society. I call on mothers to pay closer attention to the welfare, safety, and well-being of their children, particularly the girl child. “Human trafficking remains a grave threat to our communities. We must remain vigilant, educate our children, speak up against suspicious activities, and work together to protect every child from exploitation.” Hope Renew Perhaps the most significant part of Annabel’s rescue is what comes next. Okotete’s foundation is championing her return to school to rebuild her aspirations. The teenager has already expressed her ambition: to become a nurse. That dream has also received the backing of the Chairman of Ughelli North LG, Olorogun Jaro Egbo, who received Annabel from Okotete. “I am overjoyed that our daughter, Annabel, is back,” he said. Egbo said the community’s response to Annabel’s ordeal demonstrated what collective action could achieve when the safety of a vulnerable person became a shared responsibility. We are going to get her back to school. She wants to be a nurse so that she can also take care of others,” he underscored. “I call on other people elsewhere… parents should be very, very mindful of their children,” he emphasised. Back in her community, Annabel was reunited with her parents and a joyful community who agreed that she should undergo medical examinations and receive the necessary support for reintegration. “We’ll try our best to integrate her back into society and give her all necessary support,” Okotete assured. Caution The case has revived concerns about the vulnerability of young Nigerians to trafficking, particularly through promises of opportunities outside their communities. Annabel’s ordeal is therefore both a rescue story and a warning. A teenager left home, apparently without her parents knowing, only to find herself in a foreign country facing pressure to enter prostitution. Her refusal placed her in an even more precarious position, leaving her stranded until a chance encounter brought her plight to public attention.What followed demonstrated how social media, community leadership, and intervention by individuals and organisations can blend to rescue the vulnerable. But the circumstances that led to Annabel’s ordeal remain concerning. For Okotete, preventing another Annabel will require more than rescuing victims after trafficking has occurred. It requires vigilance, education, and stronger family and community protection. “Together, we can fight human trafficking, safeguard our daughters, and build a future where every girl is free to dream, grow, and achieve her full potential,” she said. For Annabel, the road ahead is now different. Not another foreign street. Not another trafficker’s promise. A classroom and eventually, a hospital ward, where she hopes to become the nurse she has always wanted to be. The post ‘I WANT TO BE A NURSE’: Trafficked Delta girl finds hope after escaping Abidjan prostitution ring appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La réunion de la commission intergouvernementale russo-burkinabè aura lieu à Moscou le 16 septembre 2026
items.description: RUSSIE-BURKINA-FASO-COMMISSION-COOPERATION La réunion de la commission intergouvernementale russo-burkinabè aura lieu à Moscou le 16 septembre 2026 Ouagadougou, 11 août 2026 (AIB) – La première séance de la commission intergouvernementale russo-burkinabè pour la coopération économique, commerciale, scientifique et technique aura lieu le 16 septembre 2026 à Moscou, a fait savoir le ministère russe de l’Énergie, à l’issue d’une réunion de la délégation russe au sein de la commission. « Les participants ont discuté des axes prioritaires de la coopération bilatérale et des questions liées à l’organisation de la première réunion de la commission intergouvernementale russo-burkinabè, qui se tiendra à Moscou le 16 septembre 2026 », indique le communiqué publié à l’issue de la rencontre. Comme précisé, les questions relatives au développement de la base juridique et contractuelle, à la coopération commerciale et économique, à l’énergie, à l’industrie, à l’agriculture, à l’éducation, ainsi qu’à la santé publique et à la prévention des épidémies ont également été abordées. La Russie est également prête à proposer des solutions technologiques pour le développement et la modernisation des infrastructures électriques du Burkina Faso et d’autres pays du continent africain. Parmi les axes prometteurs de la coopération industrielle figurent la construction de machines agricoles, les systèmes d’aviation civile sans pilote et l’industrie pharmaceutique. Actuellement, 72 étudiants burkinabè font leurs études dans des universités russes et, d’ici à la fin de l’année, l’Université fédérale du Sud (SFedU) prévoit d’envoyer des professeurs de russe dans le pays. Agence d’information du Burkina Source: TASS

items.title: CAN féminine 2026 : le Maroc rêve de finale devant son public, voici le programme des demies
items.description: Les Lionnes de l’Atlas retrouvent le Cameroun ce mercredi 12 août au stade Moulay Hassan de Rabat, en demi-finale de la CAN féminine 2026. Après leur qualification historique pour la Coupe du monde 2027, les Marocaines veulent désormais décrocher une place en finale et continuer à rêver d’un premier sacre continental à domicile. Le Maroc poursuit son aventure à la CAN féminine 2026. Après avoir éliminé l’Afrique du Sud (2-1) en quarts de finale et validé leur qualification historique pour la Coupe du monde 2027 au Brésil, les Lionnes de l’Atlas s’attaquent désormais au Cameroun. Le programme des demi-finales Mercredi 12 août : Malawi – Algérie, 18h, stade olympique de Rabat Maroc – Cameroun, 21h, stade Moulay Hassan de Rabat Les équipes encore en lice pour les places qualificatives restantes à la Coupe du monde 2027 disputeront également les matches de barrage jeudi à Casablanca. La Côte d’Ivoire affrontera le Ghana à 18h au stade Moulay Rachid, tandis que l’Afrique du Sud sera opposée au Nigeria à 21h au stade El Arbi Zaouli. Le programme se poursuivra ensuite avec le match pour la troisième place samedi 15 août, avant la grande finale prévue dimanche 16 août. Pour les Lionnes de l’Atlas, l’objectif est désormais clair : faire vibrer le public marocain et décrocher une place en finale de la CAN féminine 2026. items.title: Ousted Syrian president Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia
items.description: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia, after convicting him over charges of “war crimes” and “crimes against humanity” during the country’s civil war. The ruling against Assad, who fled with his family to Moscow as rebels closed in on Damascus in December 2024, is the first under the transitional authorities who this year began trying figures from the former government, both in person and in absentia. Assad, who was born in 1965, became president in 2000 after his father Hafez died. Shaped in its early years by the Iraq war and crisis in Lebanon, Assad’s rule was defined by civil war, which spiralled out of the 2011 Arab Spring, when Syrians demanding democracy took to the streets , to be met with deadly force. A Syrian court also sentenced Assad-era official Atif Najib to death for “crimes against humanity” committed when he was head of political security in Daraa province, the cradle of the country’s 2011 uprising. The court convicted Najib, a cousin of Bashar and arrested in January last year, of crimes including murder, “the intentional killing of children under 15”, and “torture leading to death”. The acts attributed to him are “crimes against humanity”, the court said as it handed down “the harshest punishment against him, which is the death penalty”.

items.title: ₦1.5bn mass wedding: Kano children deserve greater investment — APC stalwart
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — An All Progressives Congress, APC, stalwart and businessman, Bashir Abdullahi II, has criticised the Kano State Government over its reported expenditure of more than ₦1.5 billion on a mass wedding programme involving 1,500 couples. Abdullahi described the reported expenditure as a “costly misplaced priority,” arguing that Kano State required greater investment in education, healthcare, employment and human capital development. In a statement made available to newsmen in Jos on Tuesday, he said while supporting vulnerable citizens remained a legitimate responsibility of government, public resources should be deployed in ways that could deliver sustainable benefits to a wider segment of the population. He said the issue was not whether the beneficiaries deserved assistance but whether the reported ₦1.5 billion was the most effective way to provide such support. “There is nothing wrong with supporting vulnerable citizens. There is nothing wrong with helping people who cannot afford the cost of marriage. “But when government spends ₦1.5 billion on a mass wedding in a state facing major development challenges, citizens are entitled to ask whether that money could have achieved a greater and more lasting impact elsewhere,” he said. The Kano State Government has said the expenditure covered medical screening, dowries, business grants, furniture, food and other essential items provided to the couples. Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf said the government gave each bride ₦100,000 as dowry and another ₦100,000 as a capital grant, alongside household furniture and other necessities. Yusuf described the programme as one of his administration’s key campaign promises, saying it was designed to support vulnerable residents, strengthen families and promote social stability. However, Abdullahi urged the government to look beyond the immediate benefits of the programme and consider its long-term development impact. He argued that a one-off intervention could provide immediate relief without addressing the underlying economic challenges confronting beneficiaries. “Marriage comes with responsibilities that last for years. Families need food, housing, healthcare and education for their children. “A government that wants to fight poverty must therefore think beyond the wedding ceremony and invest in the economic capacity of families to sustain themselves,” he said. Abdullahi said the reported ₦1.5 billion could, in his view, have been channelled into classroom construction, teacher training, school feeding, healthcare, vocational education and youth employment. He argued that such investments had the potential to benefit citizens over a longer period. “A classroom remains after the ceremony. “A trained teacher can educate generations of children. “A young person equipped with a useful skill can earn an income and support a family. “These are investments that create lasting capacity,” he said. The APC stalwart stressed that his criticism was not directed at marriage or the beneficiaries of the programme. “This is not an argument against marriage. It is not an argument against helping widows, divorcees or poor families. “It is an argument about priorities and opportunity cost,” he said. He urged the Kano State Government to provide details of the expenditure and explain the long-term development outcomes expected from the programme. According to him, the government should demonstrate how many beneficiaries are expected to become economically independent, how many businesses would be established and the mechanisms put in place to monitor the programme after the initial assistance. Abdullahi also urged governments in the North to give greater attention to education and human capital development, arguing that poverty could not be sustainably addressed through short-term interventions alone. He said Kano’s development challenges required sustained investment in schools, teachers, healthcare, skills acquisition, infrastructure and productive employment. “Government must learn to distinguish between what is politically attractive and what is developmentally necessary. “A mass wedding may provide a new beginning for individual couples, but a good school can provide a new beginning for an entire generation,” he said. According to the Kano State Government, the mass wedding involved 1,500 couples drawn from the state’s 44 Local Government Areas and was coordinated by the Kano State Hisbah Board. The government also said the beneficiaries underwent medical screening and counselling before the ceremonies. Abdullahi said the programme should ultimately be assessed not by the scale of the ceremony but by the long-term improvement it brought to the lives of the beneficiaries. He added that social intervention programmes should combine immediate assistance with sustainable livelihood opportunities. “The real question is not how many weddings government can sponsor. “The real question is how many lives it can permanently transform,” he said. The post ₦1.5bn mass wedding: Kano children deserve greater investment — APC stalwart appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Delta federal roads: Gridlock, anguish as farmers, motorists groan
items.description: By Ochuko Akuopha EBU — Farmers and traders in the Ebu community in Oshimili North Local Government Area, Delta State, have been cut off from major markets across the South-South and Northern regions as the Asaba-Ugbolu-Illah-Ebu federal highway has become virtually impassable due to persistent neglect and torrential rains at the peak of the rainy season. The critical single-lane road, which serves as a primary gateway to Edo, Kogi, and the vast expanse of Northern Nigeria, has severely restricted the movement of agricultural produce and essential goods, triggering a fresh wave of economic hardship for the agrarian community. A Road That Swallows Dreams Drive through this corridor and you’ll witness a scene that defies belief. Where smooth asphalt once carried the hopes of traders and transporters, there now yawn deep gullies, potholes that have spread into muddy graves for vehicles. Heavy-duty trucks lie on their sides, their loads scattered, their drivers cursing the fate that brought them here. “My brother, for the past four months, it has been a nightmare,” said Azuka, a transporter who has plied the route for fifteen years, his eyes betraying the exhaustion of countless sleepless nights spent stranded on this road. He gestured toward a section where three trailers have crashed into each other, creating a metal sculpture of frustration. “Most drivers have decided not to follow the road anymore. We have broken down trailers everywhere.” The statistics tell a grim story. A journey that once cost a passenger N1000 now demands N5000 and that’s if you can find a transporter willing to risk the journey at all. The cost of repairs has become prohibitive, and many vehicles simply give up, joining the growing number of abandoned cars along the roadside. Farmers Bearing the Heaviest Load But the human toll transcends economics. It is measured in the faces of farmers whose yams, cassava, maize, plantain, and potatoes rot in their fields because they cannot reach the markets of Asaba, Ugbolu, and Onitsha. “The situation of the road is actually disturbing,” Mr. Andrew Onlaye, an indigene of Illah community, told NDV. “The neighbouring communities are agrarian communities that cultivate yam, cassava, maize, plantain, potatoes. The deplorable nature of the road has made it difficult for the farmers to take their goods to the market,” he added. What the farmers have cultivated with their sweat and prayers now becomes a source of anguish. The road that should carry their produce to hungry markets instead swallows their livelihoods whole. A Highway of Tears But the most devastating cost cannot be counted in naira or kobo. It is measured in lives lost, in families shattered, in dreams that ended on this stretch of asphalt. “In fact, more than two, three deaths were recorded because of the heavy duty trucks on the road. Many youths have been involved in accidents because of the deplorable nature of the road. Okada versus trailer, it killed some of them instantly. Some of them were maimed and injured. Some of the cases are still being discussed in the police station,” Onlaye revealed. The road has become a predator. When trucks fall, when Okadas collide with trailers and when vehicles break down in the middle of nowhere, the darkness descends and with it. “Because of the inability to pass through the road, it is very easy for people to fall victim to bandits, armed robbers and others attack,” Onlaye added, painting a picture of a community under siege from all sides. The Politics of Neglect As the rainy season intensifies; the road continues to steadily worsen. The heavy-duty trucks that the road was never designed to handle have accelerated its collapse. Four months ago, there were still stretches where drivers could find relief but this is no longer possible. “The trailers are using the road too often,” Onlaye explained. “The heavy duty trucks passing through the roads especially during this rainy season have made the situation worse to the extent that small vehicles cannot pass through. It is not easy to maintain vehicles after passing through the roads.” Mr. Nathan Oswe, another road user, expresses fears that the communities could be completely cut off. “Even during the electioneering period, many places may not be accessed and INEC officials may not be able to move election materials to the affected areas.” A Cry for Help The people have not suffered in silence, they have raised their voices to the Federal Government, cried out to the state government and prayed for intervention. “These are some of the reasons why the people are crying out,” Onlaye said. “When the people are crying to the Federal Government, they are also crying to the state government to intervene and do some palliative to enable the people in the community to move with ease.” “We need the federal and state government to come to our aid to see if they can do any palliative work, because transportation is the only way we can fend for ourselves,” Azuka added. A Glimmer of Hope When contacted, former Controller of the Federal Ministry of Works in Delta State, Mr. Matthew Ogar offered these words: “We are trying to see what we can do on that road; the road is under design.” However, the question that haunts every traveller and every farmer, who must navigate this treacherous path, is not whether the road will be fixed, but whether it will be fixed before more lives are lost, more dreams are shattered and before another community is cut off from the nation it serves. The post Delta federal roads: Gridlock, anguish as farmers, motorists groan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tourism Ministry to host maiden Africa Festival of Arts and Creatives
items.description: The Ministry of Tourism, Culture, and Creative Arts will host the maiden Africa Festival of Arts and Creatives from December 9-12 this year to showcase the diversity and excellence of African arts and culture. Madam Ablah Dzifa Gomashie, the sector minister, speaking at the Government Accountability Series in Accra, said the initiative was expected to provide opportunities for over 20,000 Ghanaians in the tourism and creative arts sectors. She said the festival, among other objectives, would help to position Africa’s creative economy as a driver of development; promote investment, entrepreneurship, tourism, innovation, and skills development, especially for the youth and women. Madam Gomashie noted that the festival, which followed an agreement between the MoTCCA and the African Union Development Agency, would deepen collaboration and cultural diplomacy among creatives and stakeholders in the sector. “The festival will showcase the richness of African arts and culture through music, dance, theatre, film, literature, fashion… “It will strengthen Pan-African unity and global engagement by reconnecting Africa with its diaspora and protect African cultural leadership and creative excellence on the global stage and leave a lasting continental legacy while advancing Agenda 2026 through culture-led development,” she said. Highlighting progress in the sector, she noted that domestic tourism grew by over seven percent in 2025, as the ministry continued to improve tourism infrastructure and enhance local content creation. The Member of Parliament for Ketu South cited upgrades at the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park, as well as a partnership with the W.E.B. Du Bois Foundation to manage the Du Bois Centre and strengthen global visibility. She also announced a partnership with the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO) to host the Intellectual Property Conference for musicians in Africa and the Caribbean, to build professional capacity in copyright and facilitate co-creation of copyright-protected works in both regions. Plans were underway to strengthen collaboration and promote public awareness on the provisions and strategic pillars of the country’s newly revised National Cultural Policy, Madam Gomashie said. “Tourism, culture, and creative arts are contributors to jobs, revenue, and national identity… with clear results in digitisation, infrastructure, skills development, we remain committed to job creation, culture preservation, private sector partnerships, and inclusive growth,” she added.
