items.title: Engage Now Africa, Ensign Global University sensitise students on human trafficking
items.description: Engage Now Africa, in partnership with Ensign Global University, has sensitised more than 3,000 students of Suhum Technical Secondary School (SUTESCO) in the Eastern Region to the dangers of human trafficking, online exploitation and cybercrime. The sensitisation seminar, held on Friday, July 31, 2026, formed part of efforts to equip young people with the knowledge and skills needed to recognise, resist and report activities that could expose them to trafficking and exploitation. Held under the theme “Protecting Our Children; Ending Human Trafficking in Ghana,” the programme brought together experts from law enforcement, government institutions, academia, healthcare and civil society. The organisers said the changing nature of technology had created new avenues for traffickers and cybercriminals to target children and young people. They noted that fake job advertisements, fraudulent scholarship offers, online recruitment schemes, romance scams and deceptive messages on social media and gaming platforms were increasingly being used to lure unsuspecting victims. Students were therefore encouraged to exercise caution when engaging with strangers online and to critically assess opportunities presented to them through digital platforms. They were also advised to protect their personal information, verify job and scholarship offers through trusted sources and report suspicious online activities to the appropriate authorities. The organisers stressed that preventing human trafficking required sustained public education, particularly among young people who were increasingly exposed to digital risks. Experts share insights The seminar featured a panel of experts with experience in human trafficking, law enforcement, child protection, healthcare and social welfare. They included Mr Afasi Komla, Director of Engage Now Africa and an anti-human trafficking expert; Chief Superintendent Alberta Ankrah, National Head of the Anti-Human Smuggling and Trafficking in Persons Unit (AHSTIP) of the Ghana Immigration Service; and SO Salome Gene, National Acting Head of the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit of the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO). Other panellists included ASP Mrs Edith Tetteh-Charway of the Ghana Police Service; Mr Kwame Adabo, Head of the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit in Koforidua; Mrs Ama Dzifa Amankwah, an international lawyer and child protection expert; Mr Ernest E. Ewusi, Head of the Department of Social Welfare and Community Development at the Suhum Municipal Assembly; and Nana Afua Ayesua McRighteous, a midwifery officer and founder of the Ayesua Foundation. The experts provided students with practical guidance on identifying potential trafficking situations, protecting themselves from exploitation and responding to suspicious recruitment attempts. The organisers also used the programme to highlight the growing importance of digital safety in the fight against human trafficking, stressing that young people needed to understand how online platforms could be exploited by criminals. Engage Now Africa and Ensign Global University expressed appreciation to the management, staff and students of SUTESCO, the speakers and panellists, and all partners who contributed to the success of the programme. They reaffirmed their commitment to initiatives aimed at protecting children, combating online scams and cybercrime, and strengthening efforts to end human trafficking in Ghana. The organisers said empowering young people with knowledge remained critical to building safer communities where children could grow and pursue opportunities without fear of exploitation.

items.title: Council bosses must live among their people to govern effectively — Idem, C-River Commissioner for LG Affairs
items.description: By Henry Obetta THREE years into the administration of Governor Senator Bassey Out of Cross River State, the state government says it has embarked on far-reaching reforms aimed at repositioning the local government system as the true engine of grassroots development. In this interview, the Commissioner for Local Government Affairs, Chief Victor Idem, reflects on the achievements, challenges and reforms that have shaped the state’s third tier of government. Idem speaks on strengthening council administration, the Out’s plan to compel chairmen to reside in their respective local government headquarters, ongoing efforts to deepen grassroots governance, and the controversy surrounding the controversial local government recruitment exercise. It has been three years since you assumed office as Commissioner for Local Government Affairs. Looking back, what would you describe as the most remarkable achievements during this period? If I were to assess our performance over the last three years, I would say we have made appreciable progress in repositioning local governments as institutions of grassroots development. While there is still room for improvement, many councils have undertaken projects that directly impact the lives of their people, despite operating under financial and administrative constraints. It is important to appreciate that local government administration is a specialised field. Most of the chairmen came into office with little or no practical experience in public administration. Some had backgrounds in business, politics or other professions, but governing a local government requires a different set of skills. It involves managing public funds responsibly, understanding the law, engaging communities, and balancing competing developmental priorities. Naturally, it has been a learning process. Recognising this from the outset, the Ministry placed significant emphasis on capacity building. We have consistently organised orientation programmes, workshops and policy sessions to expose the chairmen and other council officials to the principles of modern local government administration. We have impressed upon them that leadership at the grassroots is not about occupying an office; it is about solving problems, responding to the aspirations of the people and ensuring that government is visible in every community. Many chairmen have become more responsive, more development-oriented and more conscious of the need to justify the confidence reposed in them by Governor Otu and the people of Cross River State. There is a widespread perception that many local government chairmen are disconnected from the people because they prefer residing in Calabar instead of the councils they administer. Doesn’t this undermine effective grassroots governance? I believe that perception is understandable because leadership is most effective when it is visible and accessible. A chairman who spends most of his time outside his local government cannot fully appreciate the day-to-day realities confronting his people. This is exactly why I must commend Governor Bassey Otu for the bold initiative he is championing. The Governor has conceived a housing scheme that will provide official residences for local government chairmen, vice chairmen, council secretaries and leaders of legislative councils in all eighteen local government headquarters. The thinking behind this initiative goes beyond providing accommodation. It is about institutionalising grassroots governance. Public officials should live where they work, interact daily with their people and have firsthand knowledge of community challenges. Governance should not be conducted remotely from the state capital. We discovered that while some chairmen reside within their councils, others shuttle between Calabar and their local governments because of accommodation challenges. Some stay in rented apartments, others in family houses, while a few have no suitable accommodation at all. Once the Governor’s housing programme is completed, that excuse will no longer exist. Chairmen will be expected to live among their people, supervise projects directly, attend community engagements promptly and respond more effectively to emergencies. That is the true spirit of grassroots governance, and we are determined to make it a permanent feature of local government administration in Cross River State. Some people believe that several local government chairmen lack the vision to initiate meaningful developmental projects. How is the Ministry addressing this concern? Every local government has peculiar developmental needs. What may be considered a priority in one council may not necessarily be the immediate concern in another. Therefore, we encourage every chairman to engage extensively with traditional rulers, community leaders, women, youths and other stakeholders before determining project priorities. As a supervising ministry, we do not simply wait for reports. We regularly monitor projects, evaluate performance and provide guidance where necessary. Our role is to ensure that councils remain focused on their constitutional responsibilities and utilise available resources prudently. Across the state, councils have continued to invest in road grading, construction of culverts, rehabilitation of rural access roads, agricultural support programmes, manpower development, youth and women empowerment initiatives, skills acquisition, transportation support and other community-based interventions. While these projects may differ in scale, they are responding to the realities of each locality. Of course, we are not suggesting that every council has attained perfection. There are councils performing exceptionally well, while others still have significant room for improvement. Our responsibility is to continue mentoring, monitoring and supporting them until every local government becomes an effective driver of development at the grassroots. There has been considerable controversy surrounding the last recruitment exercise into the local government service, leading to protests and allegations of irregularities. What is the government doing to resolve the matter? The entire episode remains one of the most unfortunate incidents we have encountered in recent times. Governor Bassey Otu inherited a local government system that genuinely required additional manpower. Acting in good faith, he approved the recruitment of only 500 workers through the Local Government Service Commission. However, investigations later revealed that the process had been grossly abused. Instead of the approved 500, more than 8,000 names found their way into the recruitment exercise. That was not only unacceptable but represented a complete violation of due process and an assault on public trust. Despite this, Governor Otu demonstrated uncommon compassion. Rather than cancelling the entire exercise outright, he approved the retention of 3,000 workers, an unprecedented gesture that reflected his sensitivity to the unemployment situation in the state. To the best of my knowledge, no administration has ever absorbed such a large number of local government workers at once. Government could not simply ignore the glaring irregularities. Consequently, the Local Government Service Commission was dissolved, its chairman and members were relieved of their appointments, while the Auditor-General for Local Governments was also removed in line with the recommendations arising from the investigations. Further findings indicated that recruitment slots had allegedly been commercialised, with desperate job seekers paying substantial sums of money into various accounts. That amounted to a betrayal of public confidence and could not be allowed to stand. The Governor’s position has remained consistent: public service recruitment must be based on transparency, legality and merit. That is the only way to restore confidence in the system and ensure fairness for every qualified Cross Riverian. Are you suggesting that those protesting over the alleged eleven months of unpaid salaries have no legitimate basis for their action? Yes, because the fundamental issue is legality. Government cannot pay salaries to persons whose appointments were never lawfully concluded. Sympathy alone cannot override due process. What makes my position even more credible is that this issue affected people close to me. Some of my relatives were among those who attempted to secure employment through unofficial channels. I advised them from the beginning never to pay anyone for government employment because any process built on illegality would eventually collapse. Today, events have vindicated that position. This administration is determined to build institutions based on integrity rather than patronage. While we empathise with everyone seeking employment, government cannot legitimise an illegal process simply because some individuals now feel disappointed. If the protests continue, what options are available to the government, and how do you intend to prevent the situation from becoming an embarrassment? The facts speak for themselves. Government has explained its position consistently and transparently. The protest, in my opinion, has assumed a political colour because the legal issues surrounding the recruitment are quite clear. Those appointments were not carried out in accordance with approved procedures, and government cannot be compelled to sustain an illegality. Governor Otu has already gone beyond what many administrations would have done by approving the retention of 3,000 workers from a fundamentally flawed recruitment exercise. That decision alone underscores his compassion and commitment to the welfare of Cross River people. Beyond this immediate issue, our focus must shift to creating sustainable employment opportunities. Government alone cannot employ every young person. That is why I continue to encourage our youths to acquire vocational skills, embrace entrepreneurship and take advantage of emerging opportunities in agriculture, technology, manufacturing and the private sector. Many of us began life from very humble backgrounds. We carried sand, moulded blocks, worked on construction sites and engaged in other modest occupations before life opened greater opportunities. Honest labour should never be despised. As more investments continue to flow into Cross River State under Governor Otu’s economic agenda, skilled and enterprising young people will be well positioned to benefit. The future belongs to those who prepare themselves for opportunity rather than merely waiting for it. items.title: Revue de presse de ce mardi 11 août 2026
items.description: Voici les principaux titres développés par la presse nationale ce mardi 11 août 2026: Assahra Almaghribia Alors que le mois d’août est généralement marqué par une hausse des températures et une relative stabilité des conditions météorologiques, des précipitations éparses ont surpris plusieurs régions du Maroc, notamment dans les zones montagneuses et intérieures. Les experts du climat et de la météorologie soulignent que ces pluies sont généralement liées à des perturbations atmosphériques locales, accompagnées de la formation de nuages convectifs orageux. Ils indiquent que le principal danger de ces phénomènes réside dans leur caractère soudain, une région pouvant rester sous un temps chaud et stable avant que des nuages orageux ne se forment brusquement au-dessus d’elle et ne provoquent de fortes averses en très peu de temps. Al Ahdath Almaghribia Le ministère de l’Éducation nationale a confirmé que la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 aura lieu à la date officielle prévue. Les cadres administratifs et pédagogiques rejoindront leurs lieux de travail les 1er et 2 septembre, tandis que les élèves regagneront progressivement les établissements scolaires entre le 3 et le 5 septembre, selon leur niveau d’études. Le ministère a fixé au 7 septembre le début effectif et obligatoire des cours dans tous les cycles, tandis que les cours des classes d’éducation non formelle et de la deuxième chance débuteront le 5 octobre 2026. Rissalat Al Oumma) Le coup d'envoi de la 14e édition du Festival International des Arts et de la Culture « Été des Oudayas » a été donné, dimanche soir, à la corniche du Bouregreg à Rabat. Ce 14e festival se distingue par une programmation artistique variée répondant à tous les goûts, tout en veillant à proposer du nouveau à chaque édition. Il entend animer la dynamique culturelle dans la ville de Rabat, encourager les créateurs marocains parmi les pionniers et les jeunes, et renforcer la communication entre les générations artistiques, exprimant son espoir que la programmation de cette édition plaise au public, à l'instar des éditions précédentes. Al Massae L’Agence nationale de la sécurité routière a annoncé l’unification de la forme et des dimensions des plaques d’immatriculation des véhicules marocains, notamment celles utilisées pour la circulation internationale, en vertu de l’arrêté du ministre du Transport et de la Logistique n° 640.26, publié au Bulletin officiel le 3 août courant. Le nouveau modèle unifié comprend le symbole MA, le numéro d’immatriculation ainsi que la lettre arabe correspondante en caractères latins. L’Agence a précisé que les anciennes plaques pourront continuer à être utilisées jusqu’à la première opération de transfert de propriété pour les véhicules immatriculés dans la série actuelle. items.title: 'Not an ordinary year': Pakistani students receive their CIE AS & A Level results for June series
items.description: Students of Cambridge International Education’s (CIE) AS and A Level across Pakistan received their results for the June 2026 exam series on Tuesday. The CIE, part of Cambridge University Press and Assessment, offers internationally recognised exams to schools in 160-plus countries. In Pakistan, O Levels (grades 9–10) cover a broad subject range, while A and AS Levels (grades 11–12) are more specialised and advanced, providing pathways to higher education in Pakistan and abroad. While almost 368,000 students of AS & A Level worldwide received their results today, over 315,000 who appeared for Cambridge IGCSE and O Level exams around the world will get their results on August 18, said a CIE press release issued on Tuesday. Over 100,000 students from over 850 schools across Pakistan sat for the June 2026 exam series for Cambridge International AS & A Level, Cambridge O Level and IGCSE this year. The most popular subjects in the country were Physics, Mathematics, Business, Chemistry and Computer Science. This year’s June series in Pakistan and other regions was marred by the leak of its AS/A Level Mathematics Paper 12 taken on April 29 , which the CIE subsequently cancelled and scheduled a re-take for June 9. Uzma Yousuf, country director for International Education at Cambridge, congratulated the learners who were receiving their exam results. “This has not been an ordinary year. Some students prepared for their examinations against a backdrop of regional tensions, uncertainty and disruption, which makes today’s achievement even more meaningful,” the press release quoted her as saying. “I hope every learner takes a moment to celebrate what they’ve accomplished,” Yousuf said, thanking teachers, parents and school communities across Pakistan who supported students. “At Cambridge, we believe education is about more than examination results. It’s about helping young people build the knowledge, confidence and skills to thrive at university, in their careers, and in life,” she added. Yousuf said CIE looked forward to continuing innovation in assessments, such as its digital exams pilot this year and modular assessment options at A Level, for better inclusivity and flexibility for students. “Entries for Cambridge International AS & A Levels rose 5 per cent on last year, reflecting the increasing global demand for qualifications that provide a trusted route to higher education,” CIE noted . View this post on Instagram Rod Smith, group managing director for International Education at Cambridge, also congratulated the students. He noted: “More students are turning to our AS & A Levels because they combine deep subject knowledge with the skills universities and employers value most.” Smith observed that this year’s “continued growth shows just how clearly that combination resonates in a world being reshaped by AI”, expressing confidence that AS & A Levels will become increasingly important in the years ahead for this reason. “Whether students choose to study at home or abroad, Cambridge international qualifications open doors to opportunity and prepare learners for success in a rapidly changing world,“ said Smith, as AS & A Levels students have the flexibility to stay in their home country to study. CIE noted that the standing of its AS & A Levels as a “route to higher education is borne out by new UCAS application data”, which showed that 98pc of A Level students who applied to UK universities in the 2025 cycle received at least one offer of a place. In parts of the Middle East, school closures caused by regional conflict meant exams could not be sat safely, affecting almost 30,000 Cambridge students, CIE pointed out. Therefore, affected schools worked closely with Cambridge to deliver Portfolio of Evidence, an established contingency method that assesses students on a range of work marked by Cambridge examiners. CIE exams are typically held twice a year, in June and November, with results released in August and January, respectively. This year, June series papers were held from April 23 to June 9.

items.title: Students warned against fake online jobs, scholarships as traffickers target young people
items.description: More than 3,000 students of Suhum Technical Secondary School (SUTESCO) in the Eastern Region have been sensitised to the growing threat of human trafficking and the increasing use of digital platforms by traffickers to target young people. The sensitisation programme, held on Friday, July 31, 2026, was organised by Engage Now Africa in partnership with Ensign Global University under the theme: “Protecting Our Children; Ending Human Trafficking in Ghana.” The event brought together experts from law enforcement, government institutions, academia, healthcare and civil society to educate students on how to identify, resist and report human trafficking. Organisers said the rapid growth of technology had created new avenues for traffickers and cybercriminals to reach potential victims, particularly children and young people. Students were therefore cautioned against fake job advertisements, fraudulent scholarship offers, online recruitment schemes, romance scams and deceptive messages circulated through social media and gaming platforms. They were advised to carefully assess online opportunities, avoid sharing sensitive personal information with strangers and verify job, scholarship and other offers through trusted and legitimate sources. The students were also encouraged to report suspicious online activity to the appropriate authorities as part of efforts to prevent trafficking and other forms of exploitation. Speakers at the programme stressed that awareness and digital safety had become critical components of efforts to protect children from human trafficking. The seminar featured a panel of experts, including Afasi Komla, Director of Engage Now Africa and an anti-human trafficking expert; Chief Superintendent Alberta Ankrah, National Head of the Anti-Human Smuggling and Trafficking in Persons Unit of the Ghana Immigration Service; and SO Salome Gene, National Acting Head of the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit of the Economic and Organised Crime Office. Other panellists included ASP Edith Tetteh-Charway of the Ghana Police Service; Kwame Adabo, Head of the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit in Koforidua; Ama Dzifa Amankwah, an international lawyer and child protection expert; Ernest E. Ewusi, Head of the Department of Social Welfare and Community Development at the Suhum Municipal Assembly; and Nana Afua Ayesua McRighteous, a midwifery officer and founder of the Ayesua Foundation. Organisers said the engagement was aimed at equipping students with practical knowledge to protect themselves and their peers from exploitation in both physical and digital spaces. They also expressed appreciation to the management, staff and students of SUTESCO, Ensign Global University, the speakers and panellists, and the Engage Now Africa team for supporting the initiative. The organisers reaffirmed their commitment to protecting children, combating online scams and cybercrime, and supporting broader efforts to end human trafficking in Ghana. They stressed that empowering young people with knowledge and practical tools remained critical to building safer communities where children can live free from exploitation.

items.title: Chief Justice urges stronger management-staff partnership to improve justice delivery
items.description: Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie has called for stronger collaboration between management and staff of the Judicial Service, saying a productive relationship between the two is critical to effective justice delivery and maintaining public confidence in the judiciary. He said trade unions and management in public institutions should not see themselves as opposing forces, but as partners with a shared responsibility to ensure quality service delivery. Justice Baffoe-Bonnie made the call at the Catholic University College at Fiapre in the Bono Region, where he delivered the keynote address at the opening of the 2nd Quadrennial Delegates Congress of the Senior Staff Association of the Judicial Service of Ghana (SSAJUG). The Congress was held on the theme: “Trade Unionism in the Service: Partnering Management for Quality Justice Administration.” The Chief Justice said the Judicial Service could not effectively discharge its constitutional mandate without a motivated, fairly treated and professionally committed workforce. He therefore cautioned against a relationship between management and staff characterised by persistent confrontation, stressing that constructive engagement was necessary to advance the interests of both employees and the institution. “The relationship between management and staff ought therefore never to be one of permanent confrontation,” he said. Justice Baffoe-Bonnie urged delegates to use the Congress to reflect on the responsibilities of both management and staff towards strengthening the Judicial Service and improving its service to Ghanaians. He emphasised that every employee of the Judicial Service, irrespective of position, contributed to how the public perceived the judiciary. “The Ghanaian who walks into a Court does not distinguish between the Judge, the Registrar, the Clerk, or the Administrator. To that citizen, all of us together are the face of the Judiciary,” he said. According to the Chief Justice, the conduct of judicial officers and staff in their everyday interactions with court users could either strengthen or erode confidence in the justice system. “Every interaction matters. Every delay matters. Every act of courtesy matters. Every lapse of professionalism matters. And every act of quiet dedication, however small and unseen, strengthens or weakens the public’s confidence in the justice system,” he added. Trade unions must contribute to institutional development Also addressing the Congress, Minister for Labour, Jobs and Employment Dr Abdul-Rashid Pelpuo said the role of trade unions had evolved beyond the traditional function of protecting workers’ interests in their dealings with management. He said modern trade unionism should also contribute to institutional development, productivity, ethical conduct, innovation, accountability and improved service delivery. According to him, unions must become active partners in strengthening the institutions in which their members work. President of SSAJUG Marilyn Suttah, for her part, commended the management of the Judicial Service for ongoing reforms aimed at improving the conditions of service of staff. She, however, challenged senior staff to demonstrate leadership and exemplary conduct in the discharge of their duties. Mrs Suttah stressed the importance of professionalism, discipline and a strong sense of responsibility, noting that staff remained an integral part of the justice delivery system. The Congress provides a platform for delegates to deliberate on issues affecting members of the association and explore ways of strengthening collaboration between management and staff to improve justice administration.

items.title: Vice President engages Kayayei association on challenges facing head porters
items.description: Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has engaged the Kayayei Association on measures to address the challenges confronting head porters and improve their livelihoods. The Vice President met a delegation from the association on Monday, August 10, 2026, led by the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Agnes Naa Momo Lartey. The engagement focused on issues affecting kayayei, including exploitation, limited access to skills training, opportunities to establish sustainable businesses, and the welfare of women and children within their communities. According to the Vice President, the kayayei phenomenon must be viewed within the broader context of migration, inequality and development. She explained that both “push” and “pull” factors contribute to the movement of people from their communities to urban centres, making it necessary for interventions to address the underlying conditions that leave them vulnerable upon arrival. Ms Opoku-Agyemang stressed that while skills development remained important, such interventions must reflect the aspirations and needs of the women themselves. She said training programmes should have a clear purpose and be accompanied by the tools, capital and opportunities required to enable beneficiaries to turn their skills into sustainable livelihoods. The Vice President also expressed concern about the circumstances of children living within kayayei communities, stressing that their welfare must remain central to any long-term intervention. She called for stronger measures to protect women from exploitation while creating opportunities that would enable them to improve their economic circumstances. Ms Opoku-Agyemang commended the Ministry for Gender, Children and Social Protection and the Kayayei Association for their continued engagement. She reaffirmed the government’s commitment to developing a more holistic response to the kayayei situation by creating opportunities, strengthening protection and supporting vulnerable people to realise their full potential.

items.title: Karachi youth jailed for one year for ‘spreading false, fabricated information’ on social media to ‘incite violence’
items.description: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Monday convicted a man of spreading false and fabricated information and sentenced him to one-year imprisonment. However, the court released him into the custody of a probation officer after he pleaded that he was the sole breadwinner of his family and the offence was committed due to “lack of knowledge and illiteracy”. Accused Muhammad Ibrahim was booked in a case pertaining to running an “anti-state” campaign on social media platforms in February 2025 to incite “attacks on oil tankers” during a Sindhi nationalist party’s protest against a project to construct new canals. Judicial Magistrate Gulraiz Memon (East) sentenced him to one-year imprisonment for committing the offence under Section 26-A (punishment for false and fake information) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) and imposed a fine of Rs10,000. Magistrate releases convict in custody of probation officer Considering his plea and quantum of sentence, the court observed: “The convict is a young man, aged approximately 26-27 years, with a clean record…[and] he has no prior criminal antecedents and is a first-time offender.” Reasoning for not sending him to jail, the judge noted that sending a young first-time offender to prison alongside “hardened criminals would frustrate the reformative purpose of modern penal jurisprudence”. “Therefore, exercising discretion under Section 5 of the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960, instead of sentencing the convict immediately to serve a term of imprisonment, it is directed that convict Muhammad Ibrahim be released on probation for a period of one year, under supervision of the probation officer, Karachi East,” the court ruled. The court released him against the surety bond of Rs100,000 and directed him to maintain good behaviour and remain law-abiding during the probation period and refrain from committing any cyber offence or engaging in “illegal online activities.” According to the prosecution, an inquiry was initiated against the accused for allegedly running an “online campaign inciting arson attack on oil tankers to cause public panic,” adding that on Feb 27, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) had raided the accused’s location and apprehended him and recovered his mobile phone. After technical analysis, it allegedly revealed incriminating posts uploaded on a Facebook account named “Imran Sindhi”, which was allegedly operated by the accused, the NCCIA claimed. They also alleged that the forensic extraction revealed stored cache data and specific digital artefacts containing subversive graphic materials attributed to “SindhuDesh Intelligent Service S.I.S inciting arson attacks targeting public oil tankers and threatening public infrastructure”. During the trial, the accused denied the allegations and claimed he was falsely implicated in this case but he did not depose on oath nor did he lead his defence witness. However, the court rejected the defence pleas and noted that the “unrebutted oral and forensic evidence establishes beyond shadow of reasonable doubt that accused Muhammad Ibrahim was knowingly maintaining and transmitting anti-state, public-disorder material via social media from his personal smart device.” A case was registered at NCCIA under Section 26-A of the Peca read with Sections 506 and 109 of the Pakistan Penal Code. Published in Dawn, August 11th, 2026

items.title: ¿Dónde habrá nubes durante el eclipse? Consulte cómo estarán los cielos y el horizonte en cada municipio
items.description: Las nubes bajas pueden convertirse en el peor enemigo de alguien que quiera ver el eclipse de este 12 de agosto. En el siguiente mapa mostramos la nubosidad prevista para las 20 horas del miércoles en cada municipio y hacia el horizonte, además del detalle de altura de las nubes. La última previsión disponible se actualizó la mañana de este martes e incorpora los datos horarios de AEMET, de alta resolución. Seguir leyendo Metodología del mapa El mapa muestra una previsión de nubosidad para la hora del eclipse en cada punto de España. La capa visible representa la nubosidad total prevista por el modelo del Centro Europeo de Predicción a Medio Plazo (ECMWF), distribuido por AEMET a través de CEPPM. Su resolución aproximada es de 5 kilómetros. Dese el martes, el mapa incorporará también HARMONIE-AROME, el modelo de alta resolución de AEMET. Su rejilla, de aproximadamente 2,5 kilómetros, permite consultar la nubosidad prevista por horas concretas con más detalle local que el modelo europeo de medio plazo. Las fichas de cada lugar combinan dos tipos de información. Por un lado la nubosidad total prevista en ese punto por CEPPM, expresada en intervalos de porcentaje; y por otro la estructura vertical media de las nubes en el municipio según AIFS , el modelo de inteligencia artificial del ECMWF, con una resolución aproximada de 25 kilómetros (distingue entre nubes bajas, medias y altas) La clasificación de las condiciones —favorable, regular o desfavorable— combina la nubosidad total del punto con la proporción de nubes bajas, medias y altas prevista sobre el municipio. El cálculo da más peso a las nubes bajas, un peso intermedio a las medias y menor a las altas. La ficha municipal no suma las tres capas de AIFS: las nubes bajas, medias y altas pueden coexistir a distintas alturas. Se muestran como una descripción de la estructura vertical prevista, no como partes excluyentes de un mismo 100%. El modo “Vista al horizonte” es una estimación complementaria. Calcula la dirección y altura del Sol en el máximo local del eclipse y toma tres muestras de nube baja AIFS en la línea de visión, a alturas aproximadas de entre 1 y 2 kilómetros. Muestra el escenario más nuboso de esas muestras. Es una orientación sobre posibles nubes entre el observador y el Sol, no una predicción detallada del relieve ni de la visibilidad exacta.

items.title: EVIDENCE: How Ghana’s Washington Embassy staff shared money extorted from visa and passport applicants
items.description: A forensic audit by the Auditor-General has revealed an elaborate scheme adopted by the Ghana Embassy staff in Washington, D.C., to share the money the embassy extorted from visa and passport applicants between 2019 and 2025. The audit, which covers operations at the embassy from 2017 to 2025, revealed disturbing details of financial and other schemes that embassy officials designed and generated millions of dollars outside approved charges. The audit report, which is available to Pledge Against Corruption , puts the total amount of illegal funds at $19.4 million, generated from 2019 to 2025, when the illicit transactions at the Embassy were uncovered and halted by the new administration. Websites and firms linked to the embassy’s IT Officer, Fred Kwarteng, were used to charge applicants $29.75 for the return posting of their visa and passport applications, when the actual charge was around $10.1. For instance, the report revealed the creation and use of the GhanaPV.Org website, which was used to mimic the Embassy’s official website and confuse unsuspecting applicants into believing they were dealing with official channels. Read Also: Forensic audit reveals how Ghana’s Embassy in the U.S. extorted $19.3m from visa and passport applicants The Auditor-General’s report said: “The audit proved that Ghanapv.org , created in September 2020, replicated official Embassy branding by using Ghana’s Coat of Arms, the name ‘Embassy of Ghana,’ and official contact details. The website redirected applicants from the Embassy’s website to pay fees for postage and application support services. Applicants were charged $29.75 for return postage and additional support service fees through the platform. The site operated under many entities related to Mr Fred Kwarteng.” According to the audit, Ghanapv.org operated under various companies linked to Fred Kwarteng, including Ghana Travel Consultancy (GTC), Secure Data Center LLC, Travel Ghana, Travel Global, Secure Document Management Center (SDMC) and MFG Technology. The audit report continued: “The domain TravelGhana.net , originally developed between 2013 and 2014 and relaunched in January 2021, offered mailing and application support services for visa and passport applicants. The platform charged $29.75 for mailing services, $67 for passport support, and $76.78 for visa support services. The website used Ghana’s Coat of Arms and Embassy-like branding between 2021 and 2024, creating the appearance of official affiliation with the Embassy.” The audit report, which cites Fred Kwarteng in other infractions, accuses senior embassy officials of complicity in his activities. It said: “Email correspondence and internal records show that the activities of Mr Fred Kwarteng were enabled through financial and consular channels involving senior Mission officers. Evidence indicates that the Chief Treasury Officer engaged in actions involving welfare account transactions, payment arrangements, and operational coordination with Mr Kwarteng’s associated entities. “Correspondence also shows that the Minister (Consular) participated in and was copied on communications where private entities linked to Mr Kwarteng handled dispatch services and courier arrangements. These interactions occurred between 2020 and 2024 and involved redirecting applicants to Fred Kwarteng’s private platforms. The communications demonstrate sustained engagement between the officers and Mr Kwarteng’s activities within Mission operations,” The report said. Citibank staff queries Embassy officials over suspicious account Details of the operations contained in the appendix of the Auditor-General’s report show what appeared to have been a grand scheme to “create, loot and share,” with the active participation of senior embassy officials. The audit report reveals that the Ghana Embassy in Washington, D.C., created a bank account through which funds from Fred Kwarteng’s activities were channelled and paid to embassy officials under the guise of “welfare benefits.” Even before the then Foreign Affairs Minister, Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, ordered the closure of the account, Citibank, where the Welfare account was opened, had raised queries about the account. On March 16, 2020, Janet Maku Koranteng, the Treasury Officer of Ghana’s Embassy in Washington, D.C, wrote to Citibank about the opening of an account. In that letter, she said: “On behalf of the Ghana Embassy/Mission in Washington DC, this letter is to advise that, effective date April 1, 2020, you are requested to open a new account titled Embassy of Ghana Welfare Account.” She listed the account signers as Mary Zori, First Secretary; Genevieve Edna Apaloo, Head of Chancery; and herself, Janet Maku Koranteng. The first query from Citibank was an email from a Citibank staff member, Melissa Peredo, seeking clarification on whether the $80,000 intended to be withdrawn every quarter from the Welfare account as payment for staff welfare would be made in cash or by cheque. On September 4, 2020, another Citibank staff member, Jay Varkey, sent an email to Janet Maku Koranteng, querying her about payments into the Ghana Embassy Welfare Account. “A/c ending 9029, which was recently opened, is intended to make welfare benefit payments to Embassy staff. At the time of the account opening, you indicated that this account will [sic] be funded by contributions from the Embassy staff and also from contributions from the Embassy’s couriers. “The only funding to this account so far was from Ghana Travel Consultancy LLC by way of three checks indicated below. Is this the Embassy Courier that you indicated? “Maybe I misunderstood this part, but could you please explain what Ghana Travel Consultancy does for you? Are they just a courier service or are they actually processing the consular service applications on your behalf? Also, why are they making these payments to the Embassy? Ghana Travel Consultancy is one of the entities linked to Ghana Embassy’s IT Officer, Fred Kwarteng. Following this email, Citibank’s Jay Varkey and the Ghana Embassy’s Janet Koranteng discussed the query on the phone. After the call, Jay Varkey sent the following email to Janet Koranteng to confirm the explanation Janet had given for the payments from Fred Kwarteng’s entity: “Please confirm if this accurately summarises our conversation. The consular service applicants can choose a courier/ mailing service of their choice when they apply for passport/visa etc. They make separate payments to such courier/mailing service. These payments are not collected by the Embassy, and they do not pass through the Embassy accounts. Once the consular service process is completed, the Embassy will use the selected courier/mailing service to send back the documents to the applicants. However, since Embassy staff is doing some of the administration work that the courier/mailing service should be doing (e.g. packaging, etc.), the courier/mailing service has agreements to reimburse the Embassy a portion of the charge that they have collected towards mailing. This will vary for different kinds of applications, but it’s generally in the range of $3 to $5 per application processed. The reimbursed money is credited to the Welfare account and is used for Welfare payments to the Embassy staff. “Gana Travel Consultancy LLC is one of the courier/mailing service providers that is used. They will send reimbursements as described above to the Embassy on a monthly basis. Check 1010 is towards the reimbursements for the month of December 2019, check 1007 is towards the month of January 2020, and check 1008 is towards reimbursement for the month of February 2020.” An appendix of the Auditor General’s report shows disbursements to staff made from the so-called welfare account. In June 2021, the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, visited the Ghana Embassy in Washington, DC, and ordered the closure of the welfare account used to distribute proceeds from illicit funds. The account was closed as ordered by the Foreign Affairs Minister, but officials of the Ghana Embassy did not abandon their desire to continue with the scheme. While communicating the closure of the account to Citibank in an email on August 31, 2021, Janet Koranteng asked if another account could be opened without officially involving the Embassy. “Can the Welfare Committee open an account without the involvement of the management of the Embassy?” she asked. In a response, Citibank’s Jay Varkey said, “Citi will not be able to open/maintain the welfare account separately (under non-embassy management) as long as the purpose of the account remains the same (for making welfare payments to embassy employees).” The account was officially closed on October 10, 2021. However, the illicit transactions that caused visa and passport applicants to pay far more than they were supposed to pay continued until 2025, when the cover on the Embassy’s underhand dealings was blown, necessitating the subsequent forensic audit.

items.title: Bahrain FM congratulates Dar on Makkah defence pact, expresses desire to visit Pakistan
items.description: In a phone call with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Dr Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani congratulated Pakistan on the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Tuesday. The joint defence agreement, signed on August 7 between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. In a post on X, FO said that the two leaders spoke last night, during which Dar’s Bahraini counterpart congratulated him on the agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye and also expressed intentions to visit Pakistan in the near future. Dar, for his part, welcomed the Bahraini foreign minister’s desire to visit and expressed appreciation for his comments. FO said that during the call, DPM Dar “reiterated Pakistan’s firm commitment to promoting dialogue and diplomacy to achieve peace and stability in the region and beyond”. Both Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Dar have said the pact is defensive in nature, with the latter saying that it is also “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles. A day earlier, Dar had felicitated the nation on the agreement’s signing. The foreign minister noted that the term of treating an attack on one of them as an attack against all three was “consistent with the inherent right of individual and collective self-defence under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter”. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”. Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

items.description: BURKINA-KOURITTENGA-KARATE Kourittenga : La 5e édition de « Open de Koupéla » met en lumière les talents du karaté Koupéla, 9 août 2026 (AIB)-La finale de la 5e édition du tournoi de karaté dénommé « Open de Koupéla » s’est tenue, ce dimanche 9 août 2026, au plateau omnisports de Koupéla. La compétition a réuni de jeunes karatékas issus des catégories poussin, pupille, benjamin, minime et cadet. Au total, 30 prix composés de trophées, de médailles, de fournitures scolaires et de maillots ont été décernés aux meilleurs participants. Au terme des différentes confrontations, Fadel Kaboré, âgé de 14 ans, s’est illustré dans la catégorie minime-cadet en remportant le premier prix de sa catégorie. Visiblement satisfait de sa performance, le lauréat a attribué son succès à sa préparation, à son encadrement et à ses efforts. « J’ai eu un trophée, une médaille, des cahiers, des stylos et une tenue. Comme je suis élève, cela va beaucoup m’aider et je suis très reconnaissant. Après les entraînements, quand je vois que l’adversaire que je dois affronter est plus puissant que moi, une fois à la maison, je m’entraîne pour surpasser mes capacités », a-t-il déclaré. Pour le promoteur de l’Open de Koupéla, Iliassou Wango, maître du Open Karaté Club de Koupéla, cette 5e édition s’inscrit dans la volonté de promouvoir le karaté auprès de la jeunesse et de créer un cadre permettant aux jeunes pratiquants de se mesurer et de progresser. « Au cours de cette édition, il y a eu beaucoup d’améliorations, surtout côté combats. Pour cette 5e édition, en termes de performances et de prix, l’objectif est atteint. Aux parents qui sont venus nous confier leurs enfants, je demande de toujours avoir confiance en nous et de soutenir leurs enfants. Il faut noter que lorsqu’un enfant vient pour compétir et qu’il voit ses parents à côté, cela le motive davantage », a expliqué le promoteur. La directrice provinciale de la Jeunesse, des Sports et des Loisirs du Kourittenga, Awa Nathalie Yéyé, a salué la qualité de l’encadrement des jeunes pratiquants. « Ce que nous avons vu témoigne du sérieux du promoteur dans l’encadrement des enfants au niveau du karaté. Nous avons pu assister à quelques démonstrations et cela montre que les enfants ont assimilé ce qu’ils ont appris avec leurs encadreurs», a-t-elle déclaré. Elle a indiqué que le karaté est en train de prendre de l’ampleur dans la province du Kourittenga. Cela permet à ces enfants de cultiver le vivre-ensemble, la cohésion sociale, la maîtrise de soi et la discipline. Agence d’information du Burkina AWS/HB/OO

items.title: GIS shifts to intelligence-led border security as transnational threats grow
items.description: The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) is stepping up efforts to detect and disrupt emerging security threats at Ghana’s borders as criminal networks increasingly exploit technology, irregular migration routes and weak points in border systems. The GIS says it is transitioning into a more intelligence-driven institution to confront the changing nature of transnational organised crime and extremist movements across the region. The Comptroller-General of Immigration, Mr Samuel Basintale Amadu, disclosed this in Accra at the opening of a 10-day intensive training programme on risk analysis and intelligence collection. The programme, organised in partnership with the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD), forms part of the 48-month Strengthening and Harmonizing Integrated Border Management Frameworks and Technical (SHIFT) Project. Mr Amadu said criminal networks are becoming increasingly sophisticated, operating across several jurisdictions while exploiting advanced technology, forged documents, cyber tools and complex financial channels. He also warned that terrorist and extremist groups continue to exploit irregular migration routes and vulnerabilities within border systems to facilitate movement across countries. “These stark realities demand that the Ghana Immigration Service evolves into a fully intelligence-driven institution,” he said. From border checks to intelligence The new approach will place greater emphasis on professional data analysis, early detection of suspicious behaviour and closer collaboration among security and law-enforcement agencies. According to the GIS, the goal is to enable officers to identify potential threats before they develop into serious security incidents. Head of Office for the ICMPD, Madam Amala Obiokoye Nwalor, described risk analysis as the foundation of intelligence-led border management. “Risk analysis is the backbone of intelligence-led border management,” she said, stressing the need to equip immigration officers with the skills required to anticipate threats and respond effectively. 30 officers to receive specialised training Thirty frontline immigration officers selected from key entry and exit points across Ghana are participating in the 10-day programme. Participants will be introduced to advanced data technologies and modern risk-assessment systems, with a focus on strengthening their ability to analyse institutional risks and identify potential security threats. The training forms part of the wider €7.3 million European Union-funded SHIFT Project, implemented by the ICMPD. The project comes amid growing security concerns in West Africa, including porous borders, the spillover of terrorism from the Sahel and the expansion of transnational organised crime. For Ghana, the initiative is intended to strengthen the country’s ability to identify risks at its borders while improving coordination and intelligence-sharing among relevant agencies. The GIS says building the capacity of frontline officers is critical to ensuring that Ghana’s border management system keeps pace with the increasingly sophisticated methods being used by criminal and extremist networks.

items.title: NCCIA summons 4 individuals on Sharjeel Memon's complaint in connection with Mir Raza's case
items.description: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has summoned four Karachi residents on a complaint filed by Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon over “false and malicious content on social media against him and his son” in connection with the Mir Raza Ali murder case. The NCCIA’s notices, dated August 10 and seen by Dawn , stated that the agency was “conducting an inquiry into the subject matter concerning allegations of defamation through electronic/digital means, which was initiated on the basis of a complaint submitted by Naqvi Law Associates on behalf of Sharjeel Inam Memon, son of Inamul Haque Memon”. “The complaint pertains to the alleged dissemination of defamatory and fabricated content through digital platforms, which […] has caused damage to his reputation and has attracted provisions of applicable cybercrime laws,” the notices said. All four individuals have been directed to appear in person at the NCCIA Karachi office on Aug 13 at 11:30am. The notices said the respondents were required to bring their original CNICs, relevant evidence and documents in their defence, record their statements and submit their digital devices. The NCCIA warned that failure to comply would compel the agency to initiate legal proceedings before the competent court of law. The development comes a day after Memon, through his counsel, approached the NCCIA against unidentified persons for allegedly “causing harassment” and creating false and malicious content on social media against him and his son. Memon rejected allegations that he owned the guest house in Gulistan-i-Jauhar where Mir Raza Ali was allegedly tortured and murdered , and that his son had left for London immediately after the incident and had since been moving around with a bodyguard. He said the allegations had “no factual or evidentiary basis” and were intended to malign him and his son for “extraneous political motives”. His counsel asked the NCCIA to register an FIR and proceed against those found responsible under the applicable provisions of the Prevention of Electronic Crime Act, 2016, and any other relevant law. An IBA graduate and owner of the eatery Wafflix, Ali had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar. While investigators initially focused their probe on the possibility of suicide, Ali’s family has been saying that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered. Later, a second postmortem following a controversy over his first autopsy revealed that he was shot in the back, ruling out the possibility of suicide. The counsel for Ali’s family, Jibran Nasir, had demanded that the team probing the case be changed and accused the authorities of trying to “bury the facts”. On Sunday, a new team was assigned the case, and a murder charge was also added to the first information.

items.description: BURKINA-KOURWEOGO-NIOU-EDUCATION-ANCIENS ÉLÈVES Kourweogo : Les anciens élèves de « Camarade 96 » renouent avec leur école Niou, 10 août 2026 (AIB)-Les anciens élèves regroupés au sein de l’association « Camarade 96 » de l’école de Napalgué, dans la commune de Niou, ont organisé, le dimanche 09 août 2026, une journée de retrouvailles placée sous le signe de la solidarité, de l’engagement communautaire et de la protection de l’environnement. Cette rencontre, qui a réuni d’anciens camarades autour de leur établissement scolaire, visait également à renforcer la mobilisation des membres du groupe afin de contribuer davantage aux activités de l’école de Napalgué et d'établissements voisins. Placée sous le thème « Plantons utile », la journée a été marquée notamment par une opération de reboisement dans plusieurs établissements scolaires, ainsi que par une rencontre d’échanges avec la communauté éducative. Selon Abdoul Karim Zangré, membre et conseiller de « Camarade 96 », cette initiative constitue une occasion pour les anciens élèves de renouer les liens et de réfléchir ensemble à des actions en faveur de leurs anciennes écoles. « Nous, Camarade 96, avons initié cette sortie pour tenir une assemblée générale et mettre en terre des plants dans les écoles annexes de Napalgué », a-t-il expliqué. L’opération de reboisement a concerné outre, l'école de Napalgué, celles de Sagla, Tengsobongo, et Ritegué Palogo. Elle vise à contribuer à la préservation du couvert végétal et à l’amélioration du cadre de vie et d’apprentissage des élèves. Au-delà de sa dimension environnementale, l’activité a permis de renforcer les liens entre les anciens élèves et les différentes générations ayant fréquenté ces établissements. Elle a également favorisé la mobilisation des élèves autour de la nécessité de préserver les arbres et plus largement, l’environnement scolaire. Pour le directeur de l’école de Napalgué, Saniani Nabié, l’initiative des anciens élèves ne s’est pas limitée à la mise en terre des plants. Chaque arbre planté a été doté d’un dispositif de protection afin de favoriser sa survie. « Nous prenons l’engagement, avec nos élèves et les partenaires de l’école, d’entretenir ces plants afin qu’ils puissent grandir et contribuer durablement à l’embellissement de notre établissement ainsi qu’à la préservation de notre environnement », a déclaré M. Nabié. Il a invité les parents d’élèves, les enseignants et les apprenants à s’impliquer dans le suivi des plants, notamment à travers leur arrosage, leur protection et leur entretien régulier. Pour le directeur, la mise en terre d’un arbre constitue certes un acte citoyen, mais sa survie et son développement nécessitent surtout un engagement collectif et un suivi dans la durée. De son côté, le président de l’école de Ritegué Palogo, Madi Ouédraogo, a salué l’initiative des anciens élèves et exhorté la communauté éducative à veiller à l’entretien des arbres plantés. Il a estimé que ces plants constituent également un témoignage de reconnaissance des premiers élèves ayant fréquenté l’établissement. « Nous vous sommes reconnaissants d’avoir pensé à nous », a-t-il déclaré. La journée de retrouvailles s’est achevée par la remise d’attestations de reconnaissance à plusieurs membres de « Camarade 96 » qui se sont distingués par leur abnégation et leur engagement en faveur du fonctionnement et de la gouvernance du groupe. A travers cette initiative, les anciens élèves entendent ainsi maintenir les liens noués sur les bancs de l’école tout en apportant leur contribution à l’amélioration du cadre scolaire et à la préservation de l’environnement. Agence d’information du Burkina SZ/HB/OO

items.title: Nations CEO fires warning to FC Diarra ahead of CAF Confederation tie
items.description: Nations FC CEO, Kennedy Boakye Ansah has expressed confidence ahead of the club’s maiden African campaign, insisting the FA Cup winners are unfazed by their preliminary-round draw against Mali’s FC Diarra. The Abrankese-based club has been paired with FC Diarra of Mali in the opening round of the 2026/27 CAF Confederation Cup, with the first leg set to be played in Bamako in September. Nations FC will head into the continental competition after securing qualification by winning the MTN FA Cup, despite suffering relegation from the Ghana Premier League at the end of last season. Their opponents, FC Diarra, are also a rising force in Malian football, having emerged from a successful academy system and earned a place on the continental stage. The Bamako based club placed fourth in the Malian Première Division and were runners in the Coupe du Mali against league champions Djoliba who took the CAF Champions League spot. Reacting to the draw, Kennedy told Luv FM that Nations FC are embracing the challenge and are determined to make a strong impression despite facing a relatively unknown but ambitious opponent. “It’s going to be a very good experience in Africa, and Nations FC is quite a young club. Though the team has been there for a very long time ever since we took over under the good leadership of Dr. Kwame Kyei, we have made some gains. “Unfortunately, there were some issues that came up, and that culminated in us getting relegated back to Division One. But just this morning, it was confirmed that we are going to play against another young team in Mali. “I’ve done my own background checks on FC Diarra, and they came out of an academy. They play at Stade Mamadou Conaté in Bamako. I have personally been to Bamako on two occasions, so I know how things work out there. “We are going to go out there, express ourselves, and make a bold statement for ourselves as well. No, we are never scared. We just have to play very well, so we’re never shaking at all,” he stated. Nations FC, should they progress, will face the winner of the tie between Niger’s AS Zam and Burkina Faso’s ASKO de Kara in the second preliminary round. “Let’s take it one game at a time. For now, focus is on the first leg.But we will take it one game at a time,” Kennedy added.

items.title: Donald Trump annonce qu’il réclamera des "compensations" à l'Iran
items.description: Le président américain, Donald Trump, a annoncé lundi qu’il compte réclamer des « compensations » à l’Iran pour les personnes tuées et blessées dans des conflits impliquant de près ou de loin le régime de Téhéran, en réponse à une demande similaire de responsables iraniens pour les dommages subis durant le conflit. « Je constate que les représentants de la République islamique d’Iran réclament une compensation pour les dommages subis au cours du conflit militaire des cinq derniers mois (qui a éclaté parce qu’ILS NE DISPOSERONT PAS D’ARME NUCLÉAIRE), alors que cela n’a jamais été évoqué lors de nos négociations ou réunions ! », a écrit M. Trump sur son réseau Truth social. Le président américain a estimé que cette demande constituait néanmoins « une idée intéressante », qui le pousse à réclamer à son tour une compensation à l’Iran pour les personnes tuées et gravement blessées lors de différents conflits impliquant Téhéran. « Je réclame à mon tour une compensation à l’Iran pour toutes les personnes qu’ils ont tuées et gravement blessées avec leurs bombes placées en bord de route et lors des nombreux conflits », a écrit M. Trump. Le locataire de la Maison Blanche a également appelé à une indemnisation pour les familles de « centaines de milliers de manifestants innocents » tués par l’Iran au cours des 50 dernières années, ainsi que pour les 52.000 personnes qui, selon lui, ont été tuées au cours des cinq derniers mois. « J’ai donné pour instruction à mes représentants d’insister fermement sur ce point lors de toutes les négociations futures », a ajouté le président américain. La semaine dernière, Donald Trump a affirmé que les discussions en cours avec l’Iran représentaient « la dernière chance » pour Téhéran de parvenir à un accord avec Washington. The post Donald Trump annonce qu’il réclamera des "compensations" à l'Iran appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Koosin/Agriculture : L’état des cultures redonne espoir aux producteurs de Djibasso
items.description: BURKINA-KOOSIN-AGRICULTURE Koosin/Agriculture : L’état des cultures redonne espoir aux producteurs de Djibasso Djibasso, 9 août 2026 (AIB)-Malgré l’installation tardive de la saison des pluies, les cultures présentent actuellement un état jugé satisfaisant dans la commune de Djibasso, redonnant espoir aux producteurs. Le constat a été fait ce dimanche 9 août 2026. Les précipitations enregistrées jusque-là se caractérisent par leur régularité et leur faible intensité. Une situation que certains producteurs jugent favorable aux sols sableux, qui dominent une grande partie de la commune, ainsi qu’aux différentes spéculations cultivées dans la zone. Dans les champs, les principales cultures mises en terre sont le mil, le maïs, le fonio, l’arachide, le haricot et le pois de terre. Malgré les poches de sécheresse observées en début de campagne, les plants connaissent actuellement une évolution jugée satisfaisante par plusieurs producteurs. Cependant, le coût des intrants agricoles demeure une préoccupation pour les cultivateurs. Le sac d’engrais de 50 kilogrammes se négocie actuellement entre 27 000 et 30 000 F CFA, un prix qui alourdit les charges des exploitations agricoles. En dépit de ces difficultés, les producteurs se réjouissent de l’état actuel des cultures et espèrent une poursuite régulière des pluies jusqu’à la fin de la campagne agricole Agence d’information du Burkina MT/AC/HB/OO

items.title: Koosin : Des acteurs communautaires s’engagent pour l’assainissement du centre médical de Nouna
items.description: BURKINA-KOOSIN-ASSAINISSEMENT Koosin : Des acteurs communautaires s’engagent pour l’assainissement du centre médical de Nouna Nouna, 9 août 2026 (AIB)-Les associations et les différentes communautés de la commune de Nouna ont participé, ce samedi 8 août 2026, à une opération d’assainissement du Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA), à l’appel des autorités sanitaires l’amélioration du cadre de prise en charge des patients. Munis de pioches, de dabas et d’autres matériels de nettoyage, les participants se sont mobilisés pour débarrasser l’enceinte du Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) des herbes et contribuer à l’amélioration du cadre de prise en charge des patients. Le médecin-chef du district sanitaire de Nouna, Roland Bama, a expliqué que cette activité s’inscrit dans le cadre de la Journée nationale de lutte anti-vectorielle. Il a précisé qu’elle a notamment permis de procéder à la destruction des gîtes larvaires, favorables à la prolifération des moustiques. Dr Dieudonné Kientega a remercié les participants pour leur importante contribution à l’assainissement du CMA et à l’amélioration du cadre de vie des malades et de leurs accompagnants. Les responsables sanitaires ont également saisi l’occasion pour sensibiliser la population sur la nécessité de reproduire cette initiative dans les quartiers, les concessions et les lieux de travail, afin de maintenir les espaces de vie propres et de contribuer à la prévention des maladies vectorielles. Au nom des responsables des associations et des autorités coutumières et religieuses, Seydou Barro et Elie Simboro ont salué la forte mobilisation des participants et leur engagement en faveur de la salubrité du CMA. Agence d’information du Burkina AC/HB/OO

items.title: L’État règle les derniers détails
items.description: Le ministre de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique, Mouhamadou Makhtar Cissé, a présidé, lundi 10 août 2026, à Dakar, la réunion nationale consacrée aux préparatifs du Gamou annuel de Médina Baye. Les différents services de l’État ont réaffirmé leur engagement à accompagner la famille religieuse pour assurer le bon déroulement de cette manifestation à dimension internationale. Les préparatifs pour le Gamou annuel de Médina Baye entrent dans leur phase décisive. À cet effet, la réunion nationale consacrée à l’événement religieux s’est tenue lundi 10 août, dans les locaux du ministère de l’Intérieur. Présidée par Mouhamadou Makhtar Cissé, la rencontre a enregistré la présence d’une forte délégation de la famille religieuse, dirigée par Cheikh Abdoul Ibrahima Niass, fils de Baye Niass, du gouverneur de Kaolack, des responsables des services centraux du ministère ainsi que de divers services de l’État. Le gouverneur de Kaolack, Guedj Diouf, a présenté l’état d’avancement des préparatifs relatifs à la sécurité, la santé, l’électricité, l’hygiène et les infrastructures. Selon M. Diouf, au plan de la sécurité routière, le comité d'organisation a demandé la mise en place d'un plan de circulation pour faciliter la mobilité dans la cité religieuse. La famille religieuse a également sollicité un renforcement du jalonnement des forces de sécurité sur les axes menant à Kaolack, ainsi que la mise à disposition de motards pour l’escorte des personnalités religieuses. Les autorités ont aussi été sollicitées pour la mise à disposition d’un hélicoptère médicalisé pour les évacuations d’urgence, ainsi que de véhicules médicalisés. Il en est ainsi du volet assainissement où le soutien de l'Etat est demandé pour lutter contre les inondations en cette période d'hivernage. « Toutes les doléances ont été recensées au niveau régional sur ces questions. Le ministère ainsi que les différents services de l’État sont engagés à accompagner Médina Baye », a assuré le gouverneur, avant d’ajouter : « Notre souhait est de voir cette édition aboutir à une très grande réussite, voire devenir le Gamou le plus réussi de toutes les éditions organisées jusque-là. » À sa suite, les services de l’État concernés, notamment les Forces de défense et de sécurité, l’Office national de l’assainissement du Sénégal (Onas), la Senelec et la Sones ont réaffirmé leur disponibilité à accompagner la famille religieuse. Le ministre de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique a particulièrement insisté sur l’aspect sécuritaire, au regard de la dimension internationale du Gamou de Médina Baye. « Les demandes de facilitation seront prises en compte, mais sous prétexte d’alléger, nous ne devons pas prêter le flanc pour compromettre notre sécurité », a indiqué Mouhamadou Makhtar Cissé, appelant les différents acteurs à en prendre compte. Cheikh Abdoul Ibrahima Niass a, au nom du Khalife Cheikh Mahi Niass, magnifié l’engagement de l’État aux côtés de la famille. Il a prié pour que le Gamou, qui célèbre la naissance du prophète de l’islam, soit une bénédiction pour tous les musulmans, mais surtout pour tout le peuple sénégalais. Souleymane WANE

items.title: L’Assemblée nationale ouvre plusieurs chantiers
items.description: Les députés, réunis en session parlementaire extraordinaire, se sont engagés, lundi 10 août 2026, à examiner une série de projets de loi relatifs au Code du travail, à la sécurité sociale et à la protection des infrastructures d’information critiques. Ils vont aussi se pencher, en procédure d’urgence, sur les propositions de loi portant sur la déclaration de patrimoine et sur l’encadrement des crédits spéciaux et autres fonds secrets. Cette session d’une durée de quinze jours devrait permettre l’adoption des résolutions portant création de six commissions d’enquête parlementaire. La première session extraordinaire de l’année 2026 a été ouverte, lundi 10 août 2026, à l’Assemblée nationale. Le président de l’institution, Ousmane Sonko, après avoir constaté que le quorum a été atteint avec la présence de 100 députés, a indiqué que l’Assemblée nationale était dans les dispositions de délibérer. Il a renseigné que l’Assemblée nationale va étudier trois projets de loi portant Code du travail, Code de la sécurité sociale et sur la protection des infrastructures d’information critiques et les propositions de loi portant modification de l’article 37 de la Constitution relative à la déclaration de patrimoine et une autre proposition de loi relative à l’encadrement des crédits spéciaux et autres fonds secrets. L’Assemblée nationale a adopté des résolutions portant création de six commissions d’enquête parlementaire relatives, entre autres, aux opérations de cession d’immeubles, sur l’utilisation par le gouvernement des mécanismes financiers de type Total return swap (Trs) et les irrégularités alléguées dans la passation et l’exécution des marchés du programme « Un étudiant, un ordinateur », entre autres. Ousmane Sonko, après avoir levé la séance, a demandé à la Conférence des présidents de se réunir pour définir le calendrier des travaux en commission et pour la tenue de la plénière. Le député Thierno Alassane Sall a qualifié l’initiative du Pastef concernant les propositions de loi sur la déclaration de patrimoine et l’encadrement des fonds spéciaux de « diversion » de la majorité parlementaire. « Des auditions sur la séquence ayant conduit à la mort d’Abdoulaye Bâ auraient été plus pertinentes. L’Assemblée nationale essaie de se prévaloir de transparence, mais elle tarde à faire la lumière sur un certain nombre d’affaires en lien avec le budget de l’Assemblée nationale qui n’a jamais été voté », a déclaré Thierno Alassane Sall. Le député non-inscrit a indiqué que l’Assemblée nationale n’est pas encore dans les dispositions de faire toute la lumière sur le salaire du président de l’institution parlementaire ainsi que les fonds politiques mis à sa disposition et le recrutement des membres de son bureau. Le député Amadou Ba (Pastef) a salué cette ouverture qui, selon lui, traduit la volonté de transparence de l’Assemblée nationale dans la gestion des fonds publics. « Concernant la déclaration de patrimoine du président de la République, c’est lui-même qui en a émis le souhait. Il a déjà déposé sa déclaration à l’Ofnac et au Conseil constitutionnel. Cependant, le texte actuel sur la déclaration de patrimoine ne régissait pas explicitement la fonction présidentielle. Il s’agit d’adapter le cadre juridique. Il ne s’agit pas de calcul politique, mais un engagement moral et une promesse inscrite dans notre programme », a déclaré le député de la majorité parlementaire. Mamadou Makhfouse NGOM

items.title: Kourittenga : 24 équipes en lice en quête du trophée de la Coupe de l’union pour la paix et le développement du Kourittenga
items.description: BURKINA-KOURITTENGA-FOOTBALL-COUPDK Kourittenga : 24 équipes en lice en quête du trophée de la Coupe de l’union pour la paix et le développement du Kourittenga Koupéla, 09 août 2026(AIB)- Le Haut-commissaire de la province du Kourittenga, Moctar Ilboudo, a donné, ce dimanche 09 août 2026, le coup d’envoi de la 13e édition du tournoi pour la Coupe de l’union pour la paix et le développement du Kourittenga (COUPDK) sur le terrain du lycée Kourita de Koupéla. Initié par l’Association pour la paix et le développement du Kourittenga (APDK), ce sont au total 24 équipes qui sont en lice à la conquête du trophée. La cérémonie d’ouverture de la 13e édition pour la Coupe de l’union pour la paix et le développement du Kourittenga (COUPDK), a tenu sa promesse à travers deux matchs disputés au terrain du lycée Kourita de Koupéla. Les matchs d’ouverture de cette compétition ont concerné en premier lieu, l’équipe KRAS Sport qui a eu raison sur l’équipe Fondation FC par 4 buts à 1 et le second match joué entre FC Sambré qui sort gagnant par 1 but à 0 face à l’équipe FC Kut-kandé. Le comité d’organisation, pour l’atteinte des objectifs de ce tournoi, initié par l’Association pour la Paix et le Développement du Kourittenga (APDK), a exhorté aux équipes participantes à cette compétition au strict respect des règles. Pour le président de l’Association pour la Paix et le Développement du Kourittenga (APDK) et promoteur dudit tournoi, François Xavier Nikiema, ce tournoi se veut de renforcer la cohésion sociale, le vivre ensemble pour la paix. Il a demandé aux équipes participantes à toujours donner sens à la phrase maitresse de cette 13ème édition qui est le « Faire Play). Le Haut-commissaire de la province du Kourittenga, Moctar Ilboudo, a salué la tenue de ce rendez-vous sportif qui dure treize ans dans le Kourittenga, visant la promotion du vivre ensemble et pour la paix.
