items.title: Digitalisation des services à domicile en Algérie : la révolution silencieuse qui simplifie le quotidien des ménages
items.description: Trouver un professionnel disponible, qualifié et digne de confiance pour un dépannage en urgence ou une prestation à domicile a longtemps relevé du défi pour les ménages algériens. Entre le bouche-à-oreille informel, les agendas surchargés et le manque de transparence sur la qualité ou les prix, le secteur des services de proximité pâtissait d'une réelle fragmentation. Cependant, sous l'impulsion de l'usage massif des smartphones et du changement des habitudes de consommation, le marché vit une transformation profonde. Au cœur de cette mutation, les applications mobiles spécialisées réinventent la relation entre particuliers et prestataires, apportant structure, sécurité et rapidité. Un marché en pleine mutation tiré par la confiance numérique En Algérie, la démocratisation des smartphones a profondément modifié l'accès aux services au quotidien. Les habitudes ont radicalement évolué : aujourd'hui, réserver un VTC pour se déplacer, commander un repas livré à domicile ou rechercher un emploi via des applications dédiées est devenu un réflexe naturel et ancré dans le quotidien des Algériens. Forts de ces expériences réussies, les utilisateurs accordent désormais une réelle confiance aux solutions numériques pour simplifier leur vie. C'est en toute logique que cette dynamique s'étend aujourd'hui au secteur des services à domicile. Là où il fallait autrefois attendre plusieurs jours ou multiplier les appels pour obtenir un simple devis, les outils digitaux permettent désormais d'exprimer un besoin en quelques secondes et de recevoir des propositions adaptées. Cette réactivité est devenue la norme dans un contexte urbain où le temps est compté et où la recherche de sérénité au foyer est primordiale. Face à cet engouement, de nombreuses applications et plateformes ont fleuri ces dernières années pour tenter de structurer ce marché prometteur. Mais dans ce paysage de plus en plus dense, beaucoup d'initiatives peinent à maintenir la régularité, le suivi et le niveau de vérification exigés par les utilisateurs. C'est dans ce contexte que Youchoz a su s'imposer comme la référence pionnière et incontournable du secteur. Première plateforme en Algérie à avoir digitalisé la mise en relation entre particuliers et professionnels du service, l'entreprise cumule aujourd'hui 8 ans d'expérience sur le terrain. Là où d'autres projets se sont heurtés aux réalités logistiques, Youchoz a bâti un modèle solide, porté par une croissance soutenue et une équipe dédiée de 15 personnes qui veillent quotidiennement à la qualité du service et au support technique. Accessible sur le Web ainsi que sur mobile via iOS et Android, l'écosystème s'appuie sur une double interface pensée sur mesure : une application fluide pour les ménages et Youchoz Pro , un espace de gestion complet pour les prestataires. Le dynamisme de la communauté en dit long sur son adoption par le grand public, avec un rythme impressionnant d' une nouvelle annonce publiée toutes les minutes . Sans surprise, la capitale constitue le cœur névralgique de cette activité : Alger reste la première ville comptabilisant le plus grand volume d'annonces et de demandes au quotidien. Ce succès s'explique avant tout par la réponse apportée au principal enjeu du secteur : la confiance. Contrairement aux canaux informels ou aux plateformes non modérées, Youchoz applique une politique de sécurité stricte où 100 % des professionnels sont vérifiés , notamment grâce à un contrôle systématique de la pièce d'identité avant toute validation de profil. À cela s'ajoute une transparence totale portée par un système de notation et d'avis clients après chaque intervention. L'expérience a également été simplifiée à l'extrême. Pour déposer une demande en moins de 30 secondes, l'utilisateur peut décrire son besoin par écrit ou utiliser un simple mémo vocal . Il reçoit ensuite rapidement plusieurs devis comparatifs ou peut choisir de contacter directement l'artisan de son choix via l'annuaire. L'offre ne se limite d'ailleurs plus aux travaux traditionnels de plomberie, d'électricité, de peinture ou de climatisation. La plateforme couvre désormais l'ensemble des besoins du foyer : · Entretien et maison : La réservation simplifiée de services du quotidien, comme solliciter une femme de ménage à Alger , mais aussi des prestations de jardinage ou d'aide au déménagement. · Services spécialisés à domicile : L'intervention rapide d'un mécanicien auto à domicile à Alger en cas de panne, ou la réparation de machine à laver à domicile à Alger , évitant ainsi des déplacements lourds et contraignants vers des ateliers. · Événementiel et soin : Des prestations d'esthétique, de coiffure à domicile, de traiteurs, photographes ou DJs. · Santé et éducation : Un accompagnement pour la garde de personnes âgées, des soins infirmiers, des cours particuliers ou de l'assistance informatique. Alors que l'offre applicative continue de s'élargir en Algérie, la maturité d'une plateforme se mesure à sa fiabilité et à sa capacité à rassurer les ménages sur la durée. En combinant 8 ans d'expertise, un contrôle rigoureux des profils et une technologie adaptée aux habitudes locales, Youchoz confirme son statut de leader et démontre que la transformation numérique peut être un formidable moteur de sérénité au quotidien. L’article Digitalisation des services à domicile en Algérie : la révolution silencieuse qui simplifie le quotidien des ménages est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Bittou : Rasmane Denne prend les commandes du CEG de Dema
items.description: Burkina/Bittou-Education Bittou : Rasmane Denne prend les commandes du CEG de Dema Bittou, 6 août 2026 (AIB) – Le président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Bittou, Mohamed Lamine Diabaté, a procédé jeudi à l’installation solennelle de Rasmane Denne dans ses fonctions de directeur du Collège d’enseignement général (CEG) de Dema, dans la province du Boulgou. La cérémonie d’installation s’est tenue dans la salle des fêtes de la mairie de Bittou, en présence du directeur provincial de l’Enseignement secondaire, de la Formation professionnelle et technique du Boulgou, des membres de la délégation spéciale, des directeurs des services départementaux, du personnel enseignant et des représentants des bureaux des conseils d’école. Rasmane Denne remplace à ce poste Mouni Seni, qui assurait depuis un an la direction cumulée des CEG de Dema et de Gnangdin. Au cours de la cérémonie, le directeur sortant a officiellement transmis les charges du CEG de Dema à son successeur. Dans son allocution, le président de la délégation spéciale a indiqué que cette installation solennelle constitue une première pour le CEG de Dema. « Au nom du ministre de l’Enseignement secondaire, de la Formation professionnelle et technique, nous avons voulu marquer cette installation de manière solennelle afin d’encourager le directeur sortant, de féliciter le nouveau directeur et de lui prodiguer des conseils pour la réussite de sa mission », a-t-il déclaré. M. Diabaté a invité le nouveau responsable à faire preuve de courage, d’engagement et de responsabilité afin de relever les défis qui se présentent à lui. Prenant la parole, Rasmane Denne a exprimé sa satisfaction et sa reconnaissance aux autorités pour la confiance placée en lui. Il s’est engagé à accomplir avec responsabilité la mission qui lui a été confiée et à œuvrer à l’amélioration des résultats scolaires du CEG de Dema. Professeur certifié de l’enseignement général, Rasmane Denne enseigne au CEG de Bittou depuis 2013. Il prend désormais la direction du CEG de Dema, situé à une vingtaine de kilomètres de Bittou. Son prédécesseur, Mouni Seni, professeur certifié de français et d’anglais, conserve pour sa part la direction du CEG de Gnangdin. Il a souhaité plein succès à son successeur dans l’exercice de ses nouvelles fonctions. Agence d’information du Burkina SK-DNK

items.title: Nations unies | Une juive costaricienne brigue la succession de Guterres
items.description: Une économiste juive costaricienne, qui a fait ses études en Israël et dont une partie de la famille vit dans l'Etat hébreu, est devenue la favorite pour succéder à António Guterres. Rebeca Grynspan, ancienne vice-présidente du Costa Rica, est devenue la favorite de ce début de course pour succéder au secrétaire général des Nations unies. Si elle est choisie, elle deviendrait la première femme et la première personne juive à occuper le poste le plus élevé de l’Onu. Grynspan, économiste, est actuellement secrétaire générale de la Conférence des Nations unies sur le commerce et le développement (Cnuced), l’organe onusien consacré au commerce mondial, aux investissements, aux finances et au développement économique, en particulier dans les pays en développement. Lors d’un scrutin consultatif non contraignant parmi les 15 membres du Conseil de sécurité, Grynspan a reçu 10 votes «encourageants» , devançant l’ancienne ministre guyanienne des Affaires étrangères Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett (9 votes) et Rafael Grossi, l’Argentin à la tête de l’agence nucléaire de l’Onu (7 votes). Les membres du Conseil de sécurité sont invités à voter pour ou contre un candidat, ou à exprimer une «sans opinion» sur sa candidature lors de ce premier scrutin anonyme. Le prochain tour de vote révélera si l’un des cinq membres permanents du Conseil – la Chine, la France, la Russie, le Royaume-Uni ou les USA – a opposé son veto effectif à une nomination. Une fois qu’un consensus sera trouvé entre les membres du Conseil de sécurité, la nomination sera soumise à l’Assemblée générale de l’Onu, où le candidat sera officiellement nommé. Un calendrier précis n’a pas encore été publié, mais le second mandat de Guterres se terminera le 31 décembre, et le prochain secrétaire général lui succédera alors. Ses parents ont fui la Pologne Grynspan a déclaré dans un entretien podcast en 2022 que ses parents juifs avaient fui la Pologne pour l’Union soviétique avant la Seconde Guerre mondiale, alors que l’antisémitisme s’intensifiait et que la menace nazie grandissait. Son père s’est échappé avec la majeure partie de sa famille, tandis que sa mère s’est enfuie avec ses deux sœurs, laissant derrière elle ses parents, qui furent plus tard tués pendant l’Holocauste. Après la guerre, ils tentèrent tous deux de rejoindre la Palestine mandataire mais furent détenus par les Britanniques à Chypre, où ils se rencontrèrent, avant de s’installer au Costa Rica. Selon un communiqué de presse de l’Onu de 2006, elle a étudié à l’Université hébraïque de Jérusalem, où elle a suivi des études d’économie et de sociologie. En 2020, elle a pris la parole lors d’un événement technologique israélien coparrainé par des ministères du gouvernement israélien. La sœur de Grynspan, Frida, a émigré en Israël à l’âge de 17 ans, où elle a également fréquenté l’Université hébraïque, selon un portrait familial de 2014 publié par le média costaricien en anglais The Tico Times . Le neveu et la nièce de Grynspan ont tous deux servi dans l’armée israélienne, selon le même article. Avant de diriger la Cnuced, Grynspan a été secrétaire générale du Secrétariat général ibéro-américain, qui organise les réunions annuelles des dirigeants des pays de langue espagnole et portugaise. Auparavant, elle a été administratrice adjointe du Programme des Nations unies pour le développement (PNUD), ainsi que deuxième vice-présidente du Costa Rica, entre 1994 et 1998. En 2017, Grynspan a été l’oratrice principale d’un événement organisé par B’nai B’rith Uruguay pour marquer le 79 e anniversaire de la Nuit de Cristal – les pogroms de novembre 1938 contre les Juifs et leurs biens dans l’Allemagne nazie. Des positions équilibrées sur le conflit israélo-palestinien Ses positions sur Israël, les Palestiniens et le conflit au Moyen-Orient ne semblent pas différer sensiblement de celles de la direction de l’Onu. Dans un discours de novembre 2023, à la suite de l’attaque du Hamas du 7 octobre contre le sud d’Israël, Grynspan a condamné «la perte horrible de vies civiles» tant lors de l’attaque du Hamas que lors des bombardements israéliens sur Gaza qui ont suivi, y compris les frappes touchant des civils, des hôpitaux, des abris, des écoles et des installations de l’Onu. Faisant écho à Guterres, Grynspan a appelé à un cessez-le-feu immédiat à Gaza. «Cela signifie la libération inconditionnelle des otages à Gaza, maintenant. La protection des civils, des hôpitaux, des installations de l’Onu, des abris et des écoles, maintenant. Un accès sans entrave pour acheminer des fournitures à toutes les personnes dans le besoin à Gaza, maintenant. Et la fin de l’utilisation des civils comme boucliers humains, maintenant. Aucun de ces appels ne devrait être conditionné par les autres» , a-t-elle déclaré. Sous sa direction, l’organe onusien qu’elle dirige a publié des rapports sur l’impact économique de la guerre entre Israël et Gaza. En 2024, il a constaté que l’économie palestinienne avait subi son déclin le plus marqué en temps de guerre, l’ensemble de la population de Gaza tombant sous le seuil de pauvreté. Il ajoutait que même dans un scénario de reconstruction optimiste soutenu par une aide étrangère substantielle, Gaza aurait besoin de plusieurs décennies pour retrouver son niveau de vie d’avant-guerre. Un rapport de 2025 a révélé que les restrictions israéliennes imposées à Gaza après la prise de contrôle par le Hamas en 2007, combinées à des guerres répétées, avaient vidé son économie avant même le 7 octobre. Il estimait que Gaza avait perdu 35,8 milliards de dollars de PIB potentiel entre 2007 et 2023. La dernière guerre a ensuite provoqué un autre effondrement dévastateur, avec des dommages aux infrastructures estimés à 18,5 milliards de dollars en janvier 2024. Bien que les responsables israéliens n’aient pas encore commenté publiquement la possibilité que Grynspan succède à Guterres, l’ONG de droite pro-israélienne UN Watch a décrit sa candidature comme «soulevant des inquiétudes quant à la persistance des mêmes schémas de partialité et de politisation [à l’Onu]». L’ONG, connue pour sa vive opposition aux positions de l’Onu, a qualifié les rapports économiques de «série de rapports durs et unilatéraux sur Israël, soulevant des inquiétudes quant à l’impartialité et renforçant les craintes qu’elle puisse être trop encline à s’aligner sur le parti pris enraciné du système». D’après Haaretz L’article Nations unies | Une juive costaricienne brigue la succession de Guterres est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Bangladesh, India scramble to save white-ball series
items.description: Bangladesh is scrambling to save a six-match cricket tour by neighbour India next month, with the foreign ministers of both nations roped in to try to salvage the series. Comprising three one-day internationals and three T20 matches, the white-ball series was originally planned for August last year but postponed after political relations soured between Dhaka and New Delhi. “It is being worked on at the ministerial level,” Bangladesh Sports Minister Aminul Haque said late Monday, adding talks were ongoing between the foreign ministers of both nations. Dhaka and New Delhi have been at odds since Bangladesh’s 2024 mass uprising toppled then-prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who fled to India, her long-time ally, where she remains in hiding. In February, Bangladesh refused to send a team to India for the T20 World Cup, citing security concerns. The International Cricket Council (ICC) refused Bangladesh’s request to play their matches in Sri Lanka, and Scotland was drafted in to replace them. “We want to quickly resolve the deadlock that was created around the Cricket World Cup,” Haque said. “God willing, we are hopeful that it will be resolved very soon.” India last toured Bangladesh for a cricket series in 2022 and won a two-Test series 2-0. Bangladesh won the ODIs 2-1. Bangladesh toured India in September-October 2024 for two Tests and two T20 matches, when India swept both formats.

items.title: Gov’t has abandoned most of its major promises, clinging to 2 or 3 achievements – Oppong Nkrumah
items.description: The government has abandoned most of the major outcomes it promised to deliver and is now relying on a few achievements to demonstrate its performance, Ranking Member on Parliament’s Economy and Development Committee, Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, has alleged. The Ofoase/Ayirebi MP said the government’s performance must be measured against the specific commitments outlined in its 2025 and 2026 economic programmes rather than broad claims of development. He argued that several key promises in health, education and sports had either not been delivered or had been significantly scaled back. He cited the government’s pledge to expand health infrastructure, including the construction of 600 CHPS compounds and 35 Agenda 111 projects, as well as a commitment to construct new stadia. “You were here when they said we were going to build 600 CHPS compounds in the first year, and now they said they were going to do about 35 Agenda 111s,” he said. On sports, he added: “They said we’re going to build about seven stadia in, I think, the first or second year.” Speaking on Citi FM on Monday, August 10, 2026, Mr Oppong Nkrumah said the government had failed to sustain many of the major outcomes it initially outlined. “There are only about three games in town. Everything else that they listed, literally they have abandoned it,” he said. He attributed the situation partly to weaknesses in fiscal policy and revenue mobilisation, arguing that government revenue had not increased sufficiently relative to the size of the economy to support its commitments. “The major outcomes that they listed, they’ve literally abandoned all of them,” he said, adding that the government appeared to be “just clinging onto about two or three things as evidence that their government is performing.” Mr Oppong Nkrumah said the government’s record should instead be assessed by comparing its promised programmes with budget allocations and actual implementation. He argued that political claims of progress must be tested against measurable outcomes and whether the targets set out in the government’s economic programmes were being achieved.

items.title: Three convicted for defrauding trader of GH¢38,450 through fake MoMo transaction
items.description: The Assin Fosu District Court has convicted three young men for defrauding a 26-year-old trader of GH¢38,450 through a fraudulent electronic money transaction. The convicts are 24-year-old footballers Francis Appiah and Emmanuel Oteng, alias Flow Delli, and 21-year-old Emmanuel Antwi, all residents of Assin Breku. The court, presided over by His Worship Abdul Majid Iliasu, ordered them to refund the full amount taken from the complainant, Shalean Stella Bamfo. The prosecution said the incident occurred on July 21, 2026, when Appiah allegedly contacted Ms Bamfo and falsely claimed that he had mistakenly transferred money to her. He reportedly kept her engaged in a lengthy conversation before directing her to a nearby mobile money merchant, where she was deceived into transferring GH¢38,450 through e-cash to three MTN numbers registered in the names of Saar Hassana, Rebecca Bosiako Antwi and Sarah Gyeti Arthur. According to the prosecution, Appiah later transferred GH¢6,290 to Antwi as his share of the proceeds. The complainant subsequently realised that she had been deceived and reported the matter to the Central North Regional Police Cybercrime Unit. The three were arrested at a hideout in Assin Breku following investigations involving telecommunications companies, intelligence gathered by the police and a court order. The court was also told that one of the accused admitted to the offence in a caution statement. After the court convicted the three, they refunded the entire GH¢38,450 to the complainant. In his ruling, His Worship Abdul Majid Iliasu took into consideration that the convicts were first-time offenders but warned them against returning to criminal activities. The judge cautioned that they risked imprisonment if they were arrested again for engaging in criminal conduct. He urged them to abandon fraudulent activities and pursue legitimate means of making a living. The court also commended the Central North Regional Police Cybercrime Unit for its efforts in investigating and combating cyber-related crimes in the region.

items.title: NPP demands immediate action over Ghanaian links to Asante Berko bribery case
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) is demanding swift action against individuals allegedly linked to the bribery case involving former Goldman Sachs executive and former Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) Managing Director, Asante Kwaku Berko, following his conviction by a United States federal court. The opposition party argues that Ghanaian authorities should rely on information and evidence that emerged during the US proceedings rather than starting what it considers another lengthy investigation into matters that have already been examined in court. The NPP said the case involved allegations of payments to Ghanaian officials in connection with a power plant project and insisted that the identities of persons allegedly implicated should now be subjected to appropriate legal processes in Ghana. The party said any delay in acting on the available information could undermine public confidence in the country’s fight against corruption. “People are named. These are known people. They should go and deal with them. But we have been told that they are going to investigate. Investigate what?” NPP Deputy General Secretary Haruna Mohammed said in an interview with Citi FM. Mr Mohammed further criticised the government’s handling of the matter, arguing that President John Dramani Mahama must demonstrate leadership in dealing with corruption allegations and other issues confronting the country. His comments follow the conviction of Mr Berko by a US federal jury in Brooklyn on charges arising from an alleged bribery scheme involving Ghanaian government officials and a power plant project. The case has renewed calls for Ghanaian authorities to investigate and, where appropriate, prosecute individuals connected to the Ghanaian aspect of the matter. Meanwhile, the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has commenced investigations into the Ghanaian dimension of the case, including efforts to trace funds and assets that may be connected to suspected criminal conduct.

items.title: Trump says it would be ‘terrible mistake’ to remove Infantino
items.description: US President Donald Trump says it would be a “terrible mistake” if under-pressure Fifa president Gianni Infantino was ousted from his position. Trump’s backing followed Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) issuing an open letter accusing Infantino of breaking trust “through deception” with his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal. FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company. Trump’s comments mark the first time he has come out in defence of Infantino since the FFE plans came to light on 28 July. “Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino,” Trump wrote on social media. “He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again.” The 2026 World Cup was co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico this summer, with Spain crowned champions after beating Argentina in the final. When addressing the FFE proposals for the first time on 31 July, Trump said he had not spoken to Infantino about the plans. Thrive Eternal was expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE. Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared. Infantino has a close relationship with Trump and awarded him the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize in December 2025. European football’s governing body Uefa has threatened a boycott of all Fifa competitions, as well as saying it could take legal action over the failed FFE plans. The letter issued by Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC – the three confederations representing Europe, North America, Central America and the Caribbean, and Asia – came after Fifa said there was a “concerted and ongoing effort” to “undermine” world football’s governing body and Infantino. BBC Sport understands that there have been preliminary discussions between the three confederations over breakaway competitions, should Infantino remain in his position. However, substantive talks are yet to begin, according to others. “When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned,” the letter from Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC read. While the statement did not name Infantino, sources have told BBC Sport that it should be seen as an opportunity for him to resign and leave his position with dignity. Analysis: Unclear how helpful Trump support will be By Dan Roan Sports editor The timing of Trump’s first comments on this saga is intriguing. Could it be because on Monday, the United States Soccer Federation made clear its opposition to Infantino, calling for “meaningful change”? Or is it a sign of the jeopardy that Infantino could now be in after Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC’s joint letter? Trump is known as someone who does not like to back a loser, so why did this support not come sooner, when Infantino’s position was less vulnerable? Has Infantino urged him to step in? Trump’s claim that the World Cup will be less successful if Infantino is ousted will be contested by those who believe that the tournament has become too commercialised and expensive for fans under his leadership. And the focus on profit is interesting given this crisis was sparked by a plan to raise even more money, on top of the record revenue that Fifa already enjoys. It should not come as a surprise perhaps, given the close relationship between the two men, and the fact that the investment group behind the FFE plan is run by the brother of Trump’s son-in-law. While Trump’s support will no doubt be privately welcomed by Infantino, it is unclear how helpful it will prove in shoring up support within the game. And Infantino may have hoped this backing had come sooner.

items.title: Court cannot proceed if counsel is unavailable during legal vacation – GBA to Chief Justice
items.description: The Ghana Bar Association (GBA) has appealed to Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie to ensure that judges uphold the established rules and traditions governing Ghana’s legal vacation, particularly in cases where lawyers have indicated that they are unavailable to appear in court. In a letter to the Chief Justice on Monday, August 10, the GBA said the legal vacation, which runs from August 1 to September 30, is intended to give judges, lawyers and judicial staff a necessary break from the demanding court calendar. The association, however, acknowledged that Vacation Courts may sit to deal with urgent and interlocutory matters during the period. The GBA said the longstanding practice is for Vacation Courts to refrain from conducting trials, especially where the absence of counsel would affect the effective participation of lawyers in proceedings. It therefore argued that where counsel has notified the court of an inability to appear during the vacation, the matter should be adjourned rather than proceeding without the lawyer. “Counsels are not under any compulsion whatsoever to appear before a Vacation Court,” the association said. “Once Counsel in a matter indicates their unavailability to attend Court during the vacation, even though the Court may have listed their case, it cannot proceed with the case in any way if Counsel on either side or on both sides indicate their inability to proceed with the scheduled matter in Court during the vacation.” The association’s intervention follows complaints from three law firms regarding notices directing their lawyers to appear before judges to continue hearing part-heard criminal cases during the current legal vacation. According to the GBA, such directives undermine the purpose of the legal vacation and depart from established judicial practice. It said lawyers should be given adequate opportunity to rest during the period while also ensuring that, when they are required to appear, they can participate effectively in proceedings. The GBA has consequently urged the Chief Justice to take steps to ensure that judges adhere to the established rules and traditions governing the legal vacation, saying respect for the practice would preserve its purpose and promote effective participation in the administration of justice.

items.title: Cocoa farmers urge review of Bill before presidential assent
items.description: Cocoa farmers have urged the Government to delay assent to the Ghana Cocoa Board Bill, 2026, pending wider consultations. ‎The Ghana Cooperative Cocoa Farmers and Marketing Association Limited said some provisions of the legislation could affect farmers seeking alternative uses for cocoa farms that had become economically unproductive. ‎Mr Moses Djan Asiedu, Administrator of the Association, told the Ghana News Agency that while the organisation supported measures to protect cocoa farms and sustain the cocoa sector, some provisions of the Bill required further review and public education. ‎ ‎”We have told COCOBOD that they should ask the President to hold on with the assent because there are issues of concern. The farmers do not understand the law fully, and there should be more engagement,” he said. ‎The Association’s concerns centre on provisions that grant protected status to cocoa farms and restrict their conversion to other uses without approval from the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD). ‎Mr Asiedu said inadequate understanding of the legislation among farmers could heighten uncertainty, particularly in communities where cocoa production had become difficult because of declining yields and other farm-level challenges. ‎He said information reaching farmers through social media and radio discussions had been fragmented, contributing to concerns about the criminal implications of removing cocoa trees. ‎”What they have heard is that if you cut down cocoa, you will be arrested. That is how it has been presented, and it has created anger among farmers,” he stated. ‎Mr Asiedu said the Association had undertaken engagements with farmers in Enchi, Dadieso, Asawinso and Sefwi in the Western North Region, where farmers raised concerns about how the legislation could affect their livelihoods and land-use decisions. ‎He some farmers were particularly concerned about the treatment of farms that had ceased to be commercially productive and whether replacing cocoa with other crops in such circumstances could expose them to prosecution. ‎”Nobody wakes up and cuts down cocoa trees just like that. Farmers invest their lifetime in cocoa. But when a farm is no longer yielding and a farmer decides to cultivate another crop to sustain the family, why should that become a criminal offence?” Mr Asiedu questioned. ‎The Ghana Cocoa Board Bill, 2026, which was passed by Parliament on July 30, is awaiting presidential assent. ‎The legislation grants protected status to all cocoa farms and prohibits their conversion to other uses without approval from COCOBOD. It also prohibits the destruction of cocoa trees except under approved rehabilitation programmes. ‎The Bill further prohibits mining, sand winning and other extractive or environmentally harmful activities on protected cocoa farms or within 500 metres of such farms. ‎Persons engaged in illegal extractive activities affecting protected cocoa farms or nearby water bodies could face prison terms of between 10 and 20 years, fines for each affected cocoa tree, or both. ‎The courts may also order the restoration of damaged farms or compensation for affected owners. ‎The proposed legislation comes against the backdrop of concerns over the loss of cocoa-growing areas to illegal mining and other competing land uses, with implications for the sustainability of cocoa production and farmer livelihoods. ‎The Government has said the Bill is intended to curb the increasing loss of cocoa farms to illegal mining and other competing land uses and safeguard the long-term sustainability of Ghana’s cocoa sector.

items.title: Ashanti Regional Minister cautions students against indiscipline and teachers’ attacks
items.description: Dr Frank Amoakohene, Ashanti Regional Minister, has cautioned students against acts of vandalism and attacks on teachers in their various campuses. He said the rising spate of assaults on teachers and destruction of school properties by some students as reported in the media, was worrying and there was the need for students to put a stop to it, since such behavior could derail academic work and compromise educational environment. Dr Amoakohene made the call, when he addressed students of Kumasi Academy (KUMACA) at the launch of the school’s 70th anniversary logo and cloth at the school auditorium in Kumasi. The anniversary will be held under the theme: “Shaping character, cultivating minds, and nurturing souls.” The official launch marks the formal commencement of a year-long calendar of milestone activities leading up to the grand anniversary durbar. Activities lined up include a health walk, exhibition, fun-filled games, a speech and prize-giving day, entertainment, and thanksgiving services. The global alumni associations including branches in the United States and the United Kingdom are also mobilising resources to fund critical infrastructure development on campus. They include the expansion of the school’s newly completed dormitory blocks and upgrading dining hall facilities. Dr Amoakohene stated that Kumasi Academy had long been recognised for discipline and urged students not to allow the hard-earned reputation of the school to be undermined by indiscipline. He appealed to the students to continue observing the strict standards of discipline instilled by the Baptist missionaries. Referencing a recent incident at Obuasi Secondary Technical School, where the headmaster was attacked and school property vandalised, he described the conduct as unacceptable and called for no repetition in any institution. He explained that teacher discipline did not necessarily reflect hatred, but rather, a structured approach to preparing students to become responsible and productive citizens. Mr Samuel Gato, Headmaster of Kumasi Academy, said the school had produced distinguished individuals and prominent personalities since 1957, making the commemoration of 70 years a momentous milestone deserving of celebration. He said it was a shared responsibility among contemporary leaders and alumni to organise and mark the occasion in honour of the school’s past, and therefore encouraged students, alumni, and relevant stakeholders to collaborate and make sacrifices towards the successful celebration slated for next year, 2027. The event was graced by Nana Boakye Yam Ababio II (Nkwantakesehene); Mr Amo Kamel, the MCE for Asokwa; Mr Ben Abdullah Alhassan, the MCE for Asokore-Mampong; heads of institutions; together with members of the clergy, staff, and students.

items.title: IMF urges Ghana to sustain quarterly electricity tariff adjustments‎
items.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has urged Ghana to sustain quarterly electricity tariff adjustments to reduce fiscal risks in the energy sector. ‎The sector shortfall declined to US$1.4 billion in 2025 from US$1.6 billion in 2024, but remained a significant pressure on public finances.‎ ‎The IMF said in its 2026 Article IV Consultation and Sixth Review under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) that sustained reforms were needed to consolidate the gains and improve the sector’s financial sustainability.‎ ‎“Despite progress, challenges remain in transforming the sector from a source of fiscal risks to a driver of inclusive growth,” the IMF said.‎ ‎The Fund attributed the improvement to tariff adjustments, enhanced revenue collection by the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG), reduced use of liquid fuels in power generation, cedi appreciation and increased payments to energy suppliers through the Cash Waterfall Mechanism.‎ ‎It said the sector’s shortfall was projected at about US$1.1 billion in 2026, driven largely by high collection and distribution losses and costly generation contracts.‎ ‎The report noted that the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC) reduced electricity tariffs by 4.81 per cent in April 2026 before increasing them by 3.49 per cent in July 2026 under the quarterly tariff adjustment mechanism.‎ ‎The IMF said maintaining the tariff adjustment framework was critical to narrowing the energy sector financing gap, improving cost recovery and ensuring the sector’s ability to meet obligations to independent power producers (IPPs) and fuel suppliers.‎ ‎It also acknowledged government’s efforts to reduce legacy debts in the sector.‎ ‎Net payables owed to IPPs and fuel suppliers declined to US$1.7 billion by March 2026 from US$2.1 billion at the end of 2024, following debt renegotiations and payments made through government interventions.‎ ‎The Fund said the government secured savings through the renegotiation of power purchase agreements and legacy debt obligations, while making substantial payments to energy suppliers, including those linked to the Sankofa gas project.‎ ‎It recommended strict adherence to quarterly tariff reviews, regular publication of audit reports on ECG’s revenue collection accounts and full implementation of the Cash Waterfall Mechanism.‎ ‎The report also identified increased private-sector participation in electricity distribution as a key reform.‎ ‎It said a transaction adviser had been appointed to facilitate the procurement of concessionaires, with the concessions expected to be awarded by June 2027.‎ ‎The IMF said private-sector participation was expected to reduce technical and commercial losses, improve revenue mobilisation and strengthen operational efficiency within the power distribution system.‎ ‎It stressed that achieving a financially sustainable energy sector would require continued policy discipline and reforms beyond the current IMF-supported programme.‎ ‎The Fund said a more efficient and financially sound energy sector was necessary to support economic growth, attract investment and reduce pressure on public finances.‎

items.title: Woman ‘tortured’ for taking possession of grabbed land in Sahiwal
items.description: SAHIWAL: A woman, who had taken possession of her inherited land after being illegally occupied for around 30 years, was allegedly abducted, tortured and humiliated by 12 armed attackers, including three women, at Chak 93/9-L. The victim, Mardan Bibi, got possession of her land she had inherited under Ghori Pal Scheme, with the help of Pera Force, police, revenue department and the district administration, following 30 years of illegal occupation. As per the First Information Report (FIR), registered under sections 50, 148, 149, 447, 511, 365, and 354 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) on the complaint of her son, Nomir Abbas, the attackers, armed with pistols and rifles, kidnapped Mardan Bibi, subjected her to torture, and fled on the arrival of a team of Yousafwala police, which came to rescue her. As per police sources, the land inherited by the victim had been illegally occupied by one Khudayar Baloch and others for nearly three decades. After repeated appeals by Mardan Bibi, Sahiwal Commissioner Asif Tufail ordered the revenue department, Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (Pera) Force, and district administration officials to restore possession of the land to the legal owner, Mardan Bibi. Accordingly, in an operation led by Assistant Commissioner Nouman Qasir, the land was retrieved from illegal occupants and its possession was given to the complainant. However, as soon as the officials team left the village, Khudayar Baloch, Ali, Sarfraz, Yaseen Baloch, Gulaan Bibi, Nooran, Sheenan, Allah Maafi, and their four unidentified accomplices returned with arms. The FIR says that the suspects dragged the victim by her hair, and forcibly took her away on a motorcycle, after covering her face with a piece of cloth. When her cousin Akram tried to intervene, he was injured by the suspects. However, the police, on being informed of the attack on the 15 helpline, arrived at the scene, rescued the woman and arrested six of the suspects, while others managed to escape. The police say raids are underway to apprehend the fleeing suspects. Published in Dawn, August 11th, 2026

items.title: Christians urged to balance faith with healthcare
items.description: Dr Angel Abena Tiwaa, a Medical Officer, has urged Christians to combine faith in divine healing with healthy lifestyles and professional medical care. She advised Christians not to rely solely on prayer when ill but to seek appropriate medical attention, follow professional advice and adopt healthy habits. Dr Tiwaa gave the advice on Sunday during a “Health Sunday” service organised by Resurrection Power and Living Bread Ministries International, Dansoman–My Father’s House, on the theme: “Stewarding the Family’s Health.” She said Christians could pursue health through three complementary avenues: faith in divine healing, healthy living and professional healthcare. Dr Tiwaa said while Christians could trust God for supernatural healing, they should also recognise when medical attention was necessary and adhere to medical advice. She cited James 5:14-15 and Isaiah 53:5 as biblical references supporting Christian belief in divine healing. The Medical Officer, however, cautioned against treating divine health as automatic, saying believers needed to develop their faith and grow spiritually. She encouraged Christians to strengthen their spiritual lives through prayer, Bible reading, Bible study and meditation, rather than waiting until illness or crisis before developing their faith. Referring to 1 Peter 2:2-3, John 1:12, Romans 8:14 and Hebrews 5:14, she said salvation was the beginning of the Christian journey and believers needed to mature spiritually and learn to be led by the Spirit of God. Dr Tiwaa said diet, stress and sleep could significantly affect physical and mental health and should therefore be given appropriate attention. She encouraged families to eat healthy foods, exercise regularly, get adequate sleep and manage stress. Quoting Proverbs 17:22, Dr Tiwaa said: “A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.” She acknowledged that medicine had limitations and continued to evolve but said that was not a reason to reject professional healthcare. Dr Tiwaa said patients had a responsibility to follow medical advice and seek clarification from healthcare professionals about their conditions, treatment and preventive measures. “If you have been given a gift and you cherish the giver, you take care of it well,” she said, urging parents to protect, nurture and prepare their children for the future. Dr Tiwaa said health stewardship extended beyond hospital visits and required individuals and families to take deliberate steps to protect their health. She urged families to acquire reliable health information and use platforms such as social media for health education while being cautious about the accuracy of information obtained online. Dr Tiwaa also encouraged parents to promote physical activity, including walking, make healthier food choices and reduce consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages. She advised parents to learn about children’s developmental milestones and take an active interest in their physical and developmental well-being.

items.title: Informal peace structures critical to conflict prevention – Peace Council
items.description: The National Peace Council (NPC) has underscored the importance of informal peace structures in providing early warning information to prevent conflicts from escalating into violence. The Reverend Dr Emmanuel Badu Amoah, Ashanti Regional Executive Secretary of the NPC, said community-based actors, including religious leaders, traditional authorities, local watchdog committees and other influential individuals, often had access to vital information on emerging tensions long before such issues came to the attention of formal security and governance institutions. He was speaking at a training programme for peace ambassadors drawn from 12 constituencies in the Ashanti Region. Rev Dr Badu Amoah said although Ghana had established formal peace and security structures, informal networks within communities remained a critical source of information for identifying potential conflicts and facilitating timely interventions. “Somebody in the community may tell you that tomorrow there is going to be a confrontation between the two groups. That is an informal peace infrastructure, and that information is valuable,” he said. He explained that during election periods, for example, community members who observed activities such as the destruction or removal of campaign posters, or other developments likely to heighten tensions, could alert the appropriate authorities for prompt action. Rev Dr Badu Amoah said the challenge was to strengthen coordination between informal peace structures and the formal peace architecture to ensure that information gathered at the community level was properly assessed and acted upon before conflicts escalated. He said the training programme was designed to equip participants with the knowledge and skills needed to identify early warning signs, understand conflict issues, and support intervention efforts. Participants included religious leaders, representatives of community watchdog committees and personnel from the Ghana Police Service, Ghana Immigration Service and Ghana National Fire Service. Rev Dr Badu Amoah said religious leaders were particularly important to the initiative because of their influence within communities and their ability to promote peaceful coexistence and mediate disputes. He said the Council sought to build a network of peace ambassadors who would make peacebuilding an intentional part of their responsibilities and serve as representatives of the NPC in their respective communities. According to him, the ambassadors would help address issues such as drug abuse, family disputes, communal tensions, and other emerging conflicts, while promoting the values of unity, tolerance and peaceful coexistence. “Our purpose is that if something is happening that can escalate into violence, we will not allow it to happen. We want to start the process of resolving the issue and dealing with it before we get to violence,” he said. Rev Dr Badu Amoah said strengthening community-level early warning systems was essential to protecting Ghana’s peace and stability and preventing conditions that could create opportunities for violent extremism and terrorism. He said the NPC would continue to engage religious and community groups to expand the network and ensure that relevant information from communities reached the appropriate institutions in a timely manner.

items.title: Globe Tower – A new landmark rises in Cantonments City

Globe Tower, the latest Grade A development within Cantonments City, brings premium office space and a signature third-floor restaurant to one of the capital’s most prestigious enclaves, with a limited number of floors now available to forward-looking organizations. Scheduled for completion in the second quarter of 2027, the tower marks the next chapter in a district that has redefined how Accra Works, Lives, and Unwinds. With completion approaching in 2027, only a limited number of floors remain at the very center of Accra’s most dynamic enclave. To explore the space and discuss terms, contact Goldkey Properties on 055 588 7777 or 055 588 7799, or visit www.goldkeyghana.com to arrange a private viewing. Designed by the acclaimed Magna 5 Group, Globe Tower rises from a columned ground floor through thirteen upper storeys as a contemporary institutional landmark. Its strong rectilinear form and consistent grid facade project stability, professionalism, and a global corporate presence. At its heart, a dramatic central atrium frames a suspended globe, the building’s striking visual centerpiece and a fitting symbol for organizations with national reach and global ambition. Landscaped terraces soften the tower’s scale, while the open base invites pedestrian flow and a welcoming sense of accessibility. Crafted in durable, high-quality materials with generous glazing, the building balances monumentality with light-filled, human-scaled interiors. The setting is as compelling as the architecture. Cantonments City is Accra’s most sought-after address, and Globe Tower sits within minutes of the seat of government at Jubilee House, the Police Headquarters, the United Nations offices, and the American, Korean and Chinese embassies. Accra International Airport and the Central Business District are both within easy reach, the kind of connectivity that matters to top multinationals, local corporates and institutions deciding where to headquarter. Crucially, Globe Tower is not a standalone building but part of Cantonments City, Ghana’s first branded mixed-use enclave and a fully integrated live-work-unwind environment. The district is home to Grade A buildings, supports more than 2,000 people at work each day, and provides over 1,200 secure parking bays, along with continuous power, water, security, ambulance services, and professional property management. It also includes dining, leisure and a landscaped green park lie within the enclave, and its award-winning, environmentally conscious design helps keep both operating costs and carbon in check. For tenants, it is an address that signals permanence and prestige to clients, partners and talent alike. Globe Tower is developed by Goldkey Properties, a fully Ghanaian-owned developer established in 1997 and a member of the CH Group. Over nearly three decades, Goldkey has delivered more than 300,000 square meters of residential and commercial space and built eight Grade A buildings across Cantonments City, earning the confidence of blue-chip occupiers including EY, PwC, Huawei and Vivo Energy, and collecting international, continental and national honors over the years. The Minister who disclosed this when she took her turn at the Government’s said it would also preserve historical authenticity and enhance global visibility. She reiterated that it was anticipated that the partnership would bring technical expertise, international funding, and stronger archival and research capacity, ensuring that the vision and intellectual heritage of W.E.B. Du Bois were professionally managed and globally connected. She noted that it would also deepen ties between Ghana and the African diaspora, positioning the Centre as a vibrant hub for Pan-African scholarship, tourism, and cultural exchange while reinforcing Ghana’s leadership in honoring shared Black history. She said they hoped to upgrade the Du Bois Centre to the level of the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park. Touching on Improvement of the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park, the Minister said upon assumption of office, we have subjected the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park (KNMP) to a deliberate governance and institutional restructuring. She noted that a Governing Board was constituted in October 2025 for the first time for the Park and supported by a clarified organogram and reporting structure. “The Park’s redesigned website has been active since June 2025 and now includes a virtual tour,” Madam Gomashie said. “Social media engagement has increased significantly, with Facebook followers growing from 475 to over 14,200 within eight months.” She said refresh branding and improved signage had enhanced visibility; adding that visitor experience had improved through redesigning the facility, free Wi-Fi, and installation of 25 marble benches. She said there had been major infrastructure upgrades including lighting rewiring, restoration of the musical fountain, landscaping improvements, repainting of the Park, and reinforcement of concrete drain covers with metal grids. “Energy costs an average of GHS100,000 monthly. An energy audit has been completed, transformer upgrades undertaken, and a solar transition is underway, expected to be completed before end-March.” She said plans were advanced to operationalise the Dr Kwame Nkrumah Presidential Library, in collaboration with the Ghana Library Authority; saying, “opening is expected during the 2026 Nkrumah Fest”.

items.title: Security agencies urged to act against religious hate speech‎
items.description: Adib Saani, Executive Director of the Jatikay Centre for Human Security and Peace Building, has urged security agencies to act firmly against religious hate and extremist speech to safeguard Ghana’s religious harmony.‎ ‎He said inflammatory religious statements could heighten tensions, provoke retaliation and undermine peaceful relations between religious communities.‎ ‎Mr Saani made the call in an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA) following the police’s recent invitation of an Imam to assist with investigations into allegedly religiously intolerant comments he made.‎ ‎He said the police action was necessary because of the potential of such comments to inflame religious passions.‎ ‎“I do think the invitation should have even come earlier,” he said.‎ ‎Mr Saani described the comments attributed to the Imam as dangerous and capable of evoking passions, noting that religious matters were highly sensitive and that pronouncements by religious leaders could significantly influence their followers.‎ ‎He said statements perceived as attacks on religious beliefs could trigger retaliation and counter-retaliation, potentially escalating into wider communal tensions.‎ ‎Mr Saani cited experiences from Nigeria, including the case of Mohammed Yusuf, founder of Boko Haram, to underscore the potential consequences of failing to address inflammatory religious rhetoric early.‎ ‎He urged the authorities to investigate the matter thoroughly and, where offences were established, apply the law to serve as a deterrent to others who might resort to hate or extremist speech.‎ ‎Mr Saani said religious leaders commanded significant influence and that their pronouncements were sometimes regarded by followers as authoritative, making responsible communication particularly important.‎ ‎He cautioned that inflammatory statements could be interpreted by some individuals as justification for violence and thereby create tensions between religious communities.‎ ‎Mr Saani noted that an apology reportedly issued by the Imam did not adequately address the concerns, particularly where religious teachings were invoked to justify violent responses to alleged insults against religious figures.‎ ‎He said freedom of expression should be exercised responsibly, particularly on religious matters, and stressed the need to distinguish legitimate criticism from speech that amounted to incitement, hate, intimidation or harassment.‎ ‎Mr Saani acknowledged that some individuals had allegedly made repeated provocative comments against Muslims, saying such conduct should also be examined within the broader discussion on religious tolerance and responsible speech.‎ ‎“There is a thin line between tolerance and free speech,” he said, adding that people were entitled to express their views but must remain mindful of the emotional sensitivities of others.‎ ‎Mr Saani said Ghana had largely maintained peaceful relations between Muslims and Christians despite occasional challenges and cautioned against actions that could undermine the country’s religious harmony.‎ ‎He called on religious leaders and their followers to promote tolerance and peaceful coexistence, stressing that the Prophet Muhammad had not instructed Muslims to kill people who insulted him.‎ ‎Mr Saani said his own experience, including being raised by a Muslim father who sent him to Christian mission schools, demonstrated the longstanding cooperation between the two faiths.‎ ‎He urged Ghanaians to protect that harmony as a foundation for national peace and development.‎

items.title: SHC seeks report over ‘delay’ in Mustafa Amir murder trial
items.description: KARACHI: The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Monday sought a report from an anti-terrorism court (ATC) on an application filed against a delay in the trial of the Mustafa Amir murder case. A two-judge regular bench of the SHC headed by Justice Muhammad Iqbal Kalhoro also said that the report must carry details about the progress made so far in the case at the trial court. The prime accused Armaghan, along with his accomplice Sheraz, has been facing trial for allegedly abducting and killing 23-year-old Mustafa Amir at the house of the main accused in the Defence Housing Authority in January last year as well as setting the body along with his car ablaze in the Hub area. Complainant Wajeeha Amir, mother of the victim, through her lawyer, filed a criminal miscellaneous application before the SHC against a delay in conclusion of the trial. The counsel argued that the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, provides for an expeditious trial, but despite the passage of over one-and-a-half years, there was hardly any progress in the case. The lawyer also asserted that the accused side has consistently been using various tactics at the trial court to cause an inordinate delay in the proceedings. The applicant sought directives for the trial court to proceed with the matter expeditiously. After an initial hearing, the bench sought details and a progress report on the case from the ATC at the next date, to be fixed later by the office of the court. In February, the ATC had indicated both the accused persons and directed the prosecution witnesses to record their statements after the accused pleaded not guilty and opted to contest the case. Published in Dawn, August 11th, 2026

items.title: La course à l’IA a un problème structurel
items.description: Dans un document de travail publié en juillet 2026, l'économiste de la Banque des règlements internationaux, Phurichai Rungcharoenkitkul, modélise la construction des infrastructures d'intelligence artificielle comme une course, un « contest » au sens de la théorie économique, dans laquelle quelques positions dominantes capturent l'essentiel des gains The AI Investment Race », BIS Working Papers , n° 1367, Banque des règlements internationaux, juillet 2026.'> 19 . Sa thèse centrale est que la course à l'IA « engendre une fragilité qui la mine elle-même ». Le graphique ci-dessous, extrait du rapport, présente l'une des deux facettes du phénomène : son ampleur historique. Rapportée à son niveau le plus bas d'avant « le boom », la dépense d'investissement dans l'IA est sur le point de dépasser tous les grands épisodes de boom technologique en seulement trois ans. La courbe de l'IA monte plus vite et plus haut que celle de la canalmania américaine des années 1830, de la railway mania britannique des années 1840, des Années folles ou de la bulle Internet de la fin des années 1990. Les dépenses des grands hyperscalers devraient dépasser 700 milliards de dollars pour l'année 2026 seulement, et les projections du secteur tablent sur 3 000 à 4 000 milliards pour les prochaines années. Tous les épisodes historiques cités se sont achevés par des corrections brutales. La pente actuelle n'est pas un gage de solidité, mais le signe d'une sur-construction quantifiée, qui rend les booms les plus susceptibles de se retourner. Ce phénomène est provoqué par une caractéristique typique de la course. La victoire est telle que « le vainqueur remporte presque tout » : chaque acteur investit donc massivement pour distancer ses rivaux, sans tenir compte de l'impact de sa course sur les autres. Selon le modèle calibré, le résultat est un sur-investissement d'environ 1,5 fois le niveau socialement optimal, et jusqu'à trois fois là où la demande d'IA est moins élastique. Cette dynamique a toutefois un seuil critique. Une fois que la construction atteint un certain seuil, que l'auteur situe autour de 3 000 milliards de dollars, le surplus économique net (production totale moins coût du capital) deviendrait négatif. Les projections situées entre 3 000 et 4 000 milliards de dollars placeraient donc le secteur « dans la zone des risques baissiers significatifs », écrit-il. Le capital ainsi accumulé est spécialisé. En cas de retournement, il devrait être liquidé simultanément sur un marché peu liquide, ce qui réduirait d'autant le taux de récupération, surtout compte tenu de l'endettement du secteur. L’analyse se concentre également sur un deuxième problème central, celui du financement circulaire de l’IA. Le phénomène est le suivant : un acteur prend une participation au capital d'un laboratoire d'IA en échange de l'engagement de ce dernier à lui acheter de la puissance de calcul future. La demande est ainsi « fabriquée » par ceux qui financent l'offre. Le réseau relie ainsi les hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Oracle et Meta), les fabricants de puces (Nvidia et AMD), les laboratoires (OpenAI, Anthropic et xAI) et le principal néocloud (CoreWeave). L'ordre de grandeur est impressionnant : environ 46 milliards de dollars de participations ont été effectivement déboursés, mais les engagements d'achat pluriannuels s'élèvent à 879 milliards. Ces participations croisées ne font que concentrer le risque. L'auteur réume : « Le montage financier qui a alimenté la croissance est également celui qui transmet la faillite ». En abandonnant l'hypothèse d'acteurs isolés pour modéliser le réseau réel, le rapport met ainsi en lumière une nouvelle vulnérabilité : la défaillance d'un seul laboratoire pourrait, en affectant le bilan de l'hyperscaler qui le finance, inciter ce dernier à se désengager d'un autre laboratoire, propageant ainsi la crise. Ce risque s'aggraverait à mesure que la course se poursuit. Selon la simulation, la première cascade se situerait à une échelle d'investissement de 1,6 fois le niveau optimal, la seconde à 2,3 — et la trajectoire annoncée de 3 000 à 4 000 milliards projetterait le secteur dans cette zone de contagion (entre 2,1 et 2,9). Ainsi, plus le financement passe par plusieurs laboratoires reliés entre eux par quelques nœuds « pivots », plus une défaillance locale peut devenir systémique. L'auteur note aussi que la demande potentielle en IA est « vaste » et pourrait justifier une expansion considérable de la puissance de calcul. Toutefois, il souligne que la logique de course incite à sur-construire. L’article La course à l'IA a un problème structurel est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

Lo hacen una y otra vez, esperando recibir una respuesta desde debajo del concreto. Violeta tiene 7 años y había viajado desde Bogotá para pasar las vacaciones con su abuela, Amparo. Las dos permanecen atrapadas en algún lugar que los rescatistas todavía no logran identificar . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tel Aviv’s subterfuge
items.description: THE Gaza peace plan championed by US President Donald Trump and his Board of Peace has encountered major turbulence, as the American leader’s Israeli friends have rejected the deal. On Sunday, the Israeli prime minister, after a cabinet meeting, said his military would not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas is “genuinely disarmed”. These verbal gymnastics indicate that Tel Aviv has no intention of ending its occupation of the Strip. Hamas had agreed to surrender its weapons to a Palestinian committee last month, and the disarmament process and Israeli withdrawal were supposed to take place in tandem. Trump had then said the development was “monumental”. It seems his Israeli allies do not share his enthusiasm. Israel does not play by the rules, and shifts the goalposts when things are not going its way. Hamas says it remains committed to the plan. From the Nakba to the Oslo Accords to the present day, it is the Arab side that has been expected to make all the compromises, while Israel is treated like a spoilt child and given whatever it wants by its powerful Western supporters whenever it throws a tantrum. Its rejection of the Trumpian peace plan is the latest example of this hypocrisy. Trump does not like to take no for an answer. But both in Gaza and Lebanon, the Israelis have been constantly sabotaging his attempts to end hostilities. Will the American leader put pressure on Tel Aviv to honour its pledges vis-à-vis Gaza? The excuse that Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu will not want to be seen giving concessions to the Palestinians before the Zionist state’s October elections is flimsy. Peace and rehabilitation in Gaza cannot be held hostage to internal Israeli politics. Israeli provocations and oppression had created the grounds for the last two Intifadas, as well as the October 2023 Hamas attacks . When Tel Aviv cuts off all avenues for peaceful resolution of the dispute, and commits to never accepting an independent Palestinian state, then violence will be the unfortunate outcome, as the Arabs resist by any means necessary. Sadly, it appears that Israel thrives in an atmosphere of violence, and is uninterested in peace. This is the reality unless it changes its tune on the Gaza peace plan. Published in Dawn, August 11th, 2026

items.title: Meta launches AI model as Zuckerberg champions open-weight push
items.description: Menlo Park (California): Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg called for lower US barriers for open-source AI to better compete with Chinese rivals as the social media giant released a new open-weight model on Monday and said more would follow soon. The new model, Muse Glimmer, is smaller than leading AI models from rivals and is instead designed to run agentic tasks on a Mac or PC with a single graphics card, aiming to tap demand for AI systems that run directly on people’s devices. “We’ve got even bigger models that are coming soon,” Zuckerberg said in a video post accompanying his 14-page essay titled The Future is for Everyone in which he championed spreading AI rather than leaving it in the hands of a few. “The notion AI is so dangerous that the only safe path is an extreme concentration of power seems inherently problematic.” Zuckerberg’s statement marks the latest show of support for open-weight AI, which is gaining traction as businesses grow wary of ballooning AI bills and worry about recent cybersecurity incidents involving models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta. Open-weight models are typically cheaper than leading models from the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic. Th­­­­ey also come with publicly accessible core components for easy customisation, unlike closed models that companies keep fully under their control. Those controls are in the spotlight after Hugging Face, the AI coding collaboration hacked by a rogue OpenAI model, was forced to use a Chinese open-weight model to defend against the attack because closed-source models have curbs on cybersecurity use. Chinese startups are leading the race for open-weight models, with Moonshot’s Kimi K3, Alibaba’s Qwen3.8-Max and DeepSeek’s V4-Flash rivaling the performance of top US systems. By contrast, the leading models from US developers OpenAI, Anthropic and Alphabet’s Google are closed-weight. Shares of Meta, which have fallen about 10pc so far this year, were up nearly 3pc in premarket trading on Monday. Policy rethink Meta also plans to release the weights of Muse Spark 1.2, its most advanced model, built by a costly superintelligence team it formed last year to claw its way back into the AI race. The company had long supported open models and was among the only US tech firms to release such models before poor reception for its Llama 4 last year forced a change in strategy. In Monday’s wide-ranging AI essay, Zuckerberg also unveiled a new $1 billion fund that aims to ease fears about the impact of its data-center build-out by offering support to communities. Growing local opposition to data centres has become a key election iss­ue in the US and one of the biggest hur­­dles for Big Tech’s push to build the infrastructure needed to power AI. “One significant disadvantage that the U.S. has compared to countries like China is that it is more difficult to build infrastructure here,” Zuckerberg, whose company is set to spend as much as $145 billion this year on AI infrastructure, said. Zuckerberg also said the US needed to rethink policies if domestic firms were to lead in open-weight models, including on data use and distillation — a method that uses the outputs of a powerful AI system to train a smaller model that can handle some of the same tasks with far less computing power. He said that Meta would implement a governance structure to give its independent directors the power to approve the safety criteria for rele­asing models. “Foreign labs curren­tly hold several advantages here sin­ce American labs have to comply wi­­­­­th many additional restrictions on training data,” Zuckerberg said. Published in Dawn, August 11th, 2026

items.title: Libya's NOC warns of force majeure, Zawiya refinery shutdown if drone attacks continue
items.description: TRIPOLI, Aug 10 (Reuters) - Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) said on Tuesday it could declare force majeure and completely halt operations at the Zawiya refinery if drone attacks on oil assets in the city continued, after reporting a third such attack over Sunday and Monday. NOC said the latest drone targeted an oil blending and filling plant operated by the Zawiya Oil Refining Company, falling near its main oil tank and a pipeline network used to produce oils for the domestic market. No casualties or material damage were reported.

items.title: El Gobierno y el Senado se encaminan hacia un choque institucional por las comparecencias sobre la crisis de Ceuta
items.description: La idea de agosto como un mes desierto de actividad parlamentaria parece cosa del pasado. La agitada vida política española —y mundial—, así como la sucesión de emergencias que el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez viene encadenando desde la pandemia, han transformado el escasísimo programa estival de las Cortes en uno más nutrido. Este verano, la agenda no para a cuenta del estallido de la inédita crisis de Ceuta, de la que el PP responsabiliza a La Moncloa, y encamina al Senado y al Ejecutivo hacia un choque institucional entre ambos. De un lado, el PP, con mayoría absoluta en la Cámara alta, donde ha registrado las solicitudes de comparecencia de los ministros de Interior, Defensa y Exteriores. En la otra esquina, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, Margarita Robles y José Manuel Albares, que no responderán a la cita para evitar “duplicidad” alegando que ya darán explicaciones por propia iniciativa a final de mes en el Congreso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los bulos que propiciaron la avalancha migratoria hacia Ceuta: “La puerta está abierta”
items.description: “Por la mañana vi en Instagram y TikTok vídeos de personas que atravesaban la frontera (de Ceuta) y decían: ‘La puerta está abierta”. Es uno de los centenares de mensajes, post o grabaciones analizadas por el ingeniero informático marroquí Maruán L. Alaui, que ha seguido desde el inicio la crisis migratoria de la ciudad autónoma española del norte de África. En un estudio difundido en Instagram, ha constatado que los bulos en las redes sociales que tergiversaban una sentencia del Tribunal Supremo español, sobre expulsión en caliente de los migrantes irregulares a través del mar, desencadenaron la avalancha humana.
